meta.title: Programa de Inglês Executivo
meta.subtitle: Desenho Curricular · 72 aulas · 7 módulos
meta.tagline: Regra de Exatas: segunda é a planta (teoria), sexta é a obra (prática).
meta.particularity: Feito para o seu perfil de exatas: primeiro a 'planta' da língua (estrutura, gramática e tempos verbais), depois a 'obra' (conversação e role-play). Foco em business — relacionamento, negociação e segurança do trabalho — com um eixo dedicado ao domínio dos tempos verbais.

overview: Um programa de inglês de negócios para a sua rotina de Diretor de Operações — as reuniões mensais com os maiores clientes de data center do mundo. O foco é a comunicação executiva real: apresentar a empresa, negociar custo, prazo e contrato, e tratar de segurança do trabalho com domínio. Como você gosta de entender a estrutura antes de aplicar, cada semana é um par — a teoria da língua no início, a prática em conversa no fim. E, ao concluir cada módulo, você se testa e consolida o que aprendeu.
logic: O Fábio é engenheiro e "gosta de saber como o prédio é construído antes de entrar". Por isso toda SEGUNDA é a planta da língua — TEORIA: estrutura, gramática, tempos verbais e linguística do tema da semana — e toda SEXTA é a obra — PRÁTICA: conversação e role-play aplicando exatamente o que foi visto na segunda, sempre no contexto Microsoft, Amazon/AWS e Google. Cada semana é um par Teoria → Prática. Ao final de cada módulo, o sistema gera automaticamente uma Prova de Módulo, que consolida todo o conteúdo estudado e fica registrada no material.

Aula de sexta — conversação e role-play sobre o que foi visto na segunda.
Apresentação final do diretor — um cliente big data por apresentação.

modules.name: BUSINESS SURVIVAL & DESTRAVAR EXECUTIVO
modules.objective: Bloco de abertura para destravar a comunicação executiva cotidiana — apresentar-se, abrir reuniões, fazer perguntas e dizer números, datas, valores e prazos em voz alta sem travar. Atende diretamente à fala do Fábio em entrevista — inglês "travado", troca de tempos verbais e vocabulário pouco elaborado — criando confiança antes do mergulho de negócios. Segundas trazem a estrutura da língua; sextas, a prática conversacional com interlocutores Microsoft, Amazon/AWS e Google. Ao final do módulo, o sistema gera automaticamente uma Prova de Módulo — consolidando todo o conteúdo estudado — que fica registrada no material (a inserção ocorre na etapa de produção dos conteúdos).

modules.name: CONHECER & APRESENTAR A RACIONAL
modules.objective: Capacitar o diretor de operações a apresentar a empresa como um todo — conteúdo extraído de racional.com: mais de 50 anos de história (fundada em 1971), 620+ obras, 10M+ m² construídos, solidez e robustez financeira, segmentos (saúde, shopping centers, indústria, data centers hyperscale), modelo de negócio (viabilidade → engenharia → pré-construção → construção) e o diferencial de entrega. Endereça o Pilar 1 do Fábio: estabelecer confiança apresentando os pontos fortes da Racional. Ao final do módulo, o sistema gera automaticamente uma Prova de Módulo — consolidando todo o conteúdo estudado — que fica registrada no material (a inserção ocorre na etapa de produção dos conteúdos).

modules.name: ESTABELECER RELACIONAMENTO & CONFIANÇA · PILAR 1
modules.objective: Desenvolver a linguagem do relacionamento de longo prazo com os clientes — registro formal vs. próximo, polidez, compromisso e contextualização ("explicar o porquê antes de expor"). Trabalha a relação empresa a empresa em contratos de valores expressivos, com rodízio entre Microsoft, Amazon/AWS e Google nas reuniões mensais individuais que o Fábio conduz. Ao final do módulo, o sistema gera automaticamente uma Prova de Módulo — consolidando todo o conteúdo estudado — que fica registrada no material (a inserção ocorre na etapa de produção dos conteúdos).

modules.name: NEGOCIAÇÃO: CUSTO, PRAZO & CONTRATO · PILAR 2
modules.objective: Coração do Pilar 2 — negociação comercial. Cobre custo de atividades de engenharia, valores expressivos e margem, prazos correlacionados a custo, questões contratuais (escopo, change orders, claims), tréplica (defender posição na 2ª e 3ª troca da reunião) e a segurança de execução do empreendimento. Segundas estruturam a gramática da negociação (condicionais, comparativos, futuros); sextas aplicam em role-play com os clientes big data. Ao final do módulo, o sistema gera automaticamente uma Prova de Módulo — consolidando todo o conteúdo estudado — que fica registrada no material (a inserção ocorre na etapa de produção dos conteúdos).

modules.name: SEGURANÇA DO TRABALHO, SST & CONFORMIDADE · PILAR 3
modules.objective: Pilar 3 — segurança do trabalho, tema que está sempre na mesa com as big techs. Vocabulário de SST, leitura de indicadores e dados de conformidade, normas e auditorias externas, relato de incidentes e a defesa da cultura de segurança da Racional ("Tô Sabendo", DSM, treinamentos) como diferencial competitivo perante Microsoft, Amazon/AWS e Google. Ao final do módulo, o sistema gera automaticamente uma Prova de Módulo — consolidando todo o conteúdo estudado — que fica registrada no material (a inserção ocorre na etapa de produção dos conteúdos).

modules.name: REUNIÕES, REPORT & DOMÍNIO DOS TEMPOS VERBAIS
modules.objective: Aplicar o inglês nas reuniões mensais de report e negociação — eixo dedicado aos Tempos Verbais (passado, presente e futuro), deficiência explicitamente trazida pelo Fábio em entrevista. Cobre status updates, condução de reunião, perguntas inesperadas, supply chain (área dele) e comunicação escrita. Segundas fixam a estrutura verbal; sextas treinam a escolha do tempo certo ao vivo com os clientes. Ao final do módulo, o sistema gera automaticamente uma Prova de Módulo — consolidando todo o conteúdo estudado — que fica registrada no material (a inserção ocorre na etapa de produção dos conteúdos).

modules.name: CAPSTONE — CICLO DO CLIENTE BIG DATA
modules.objective: Encerrar o curso com três apresentações conduzidas pelo diretor de operações, cada uma com um cliente big data: pitch institucional para a Microsoft, negociação de custo/prazo/contrato com a Amazon/AWS e QBR de segurança e relacionamento com o Google. Cada apresentação é precedida de uma segunda de briefing e revisão de linguagem (TEORIA) e entregue na sexta (CAPSTONE). Ao final do módulo, o sistema gera automaticamente uma Prova de Módulo — consolidando todo o conteúdo estudado — que fica registrada no material (a inserção ocorre na etapa de produção dos conteúdos).

O Fábio apresenta a Racional — 50+ anos, solidez e robustez financeira, segmentos, expertise em data centers hyperscale e a cultura de entrega — estabelecendo a relação de confiança empresa a empresa.

M1.title: Teste-se · Módulo 1 — Survival Executivo
M1.intro: Que tal medir, em 8 questões rápidas, o quanto você já destravou? Present simple × continuous, sua apresentação executiva, WH-questions e números. Vá no seu ritmo — é só para somar.

exercises.title: 1. Rotina ou agora?
exercises.prompt: "I ___ the client once a month." (rotina)

options.whyWrong: Continuous é para algo agora, não rotina.
'-s' só na 3ª pessoa (he/she/it).

exercises.explanation: Rotina = present simple.

exercises.title: 2. Em andamento agora
exercises.prompt: Right now, we ___ (build) three data centers.
exercises.explanation: 'Right now' → present continuous.

exercises.title: 3. Duração
exercises.prompt: Quero saber quanto tempo a revisão leva:

options.text: How long will the review take?
How much will the review take?
options.whyWrong: 'How much' é valor, não duração.
'When' é data.

exercises.explanation: Duração = How long.

exercises.title: 4. Question tag
exercises.prompt: The report is due on Friday, ___ it?
exercises.explanation: Afirmativa com 'is' → tag negativa 'isn't it?'.

exercises.title: 5. Frase de cargo
exercises.explanation: I am responsible for operations.

exercises.title: 6. Tempo verbal × uso
exercises.explanation: Marcadores indicam o tempo/forma certos.

exercises.title: 7. Abertura de reunião
exercises.prompt: Melhor pergunta para devolver a palavra na abertura:

options.text: How has your week been so far?

options.whyWrong: Confrontador.
Invasivo.

exercises.explanation: Pergunta leve quebra o gelo.

exercises.title: 8. Racional em uma linha
exercises.prompt: We build ___-critical projects like data centers.
exercises.explanation: 'Mission-critical' posiciona a Racional no mundo do cliente.

lessons.title: Present Simple & Continuous: estruturando quem você é e o que faz
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue estruturar quem é e o que faz na Racional usando o Present Simple para rotina e cargo e o Present Continuous para o que está em andamento agora.
lessons.overview:
Introducing who you are is the first thing a client like Microsoft, Amazon, or Google hears from you. Before talking about numbers or a contract, the person you are speaking with needs to understand your role and what you do day to day. As Operations Director of a construction company with more than 50 years of history and 620 delivered projects, you speak on behalf of a solid company, and that begins with a good personal introduction: your name, your role, and your main responsibility.

For this, English uses two verb tenses that work together. The Present Simple describes what is fixed: your role, your routine, and the facts about the company. The Present Continuous describes what is happening right now, on a temporary basis: the projects underway, the teams you are hiring. Knowing how to separate the two avoids the most common mistake people make when they still freeze up: mixing "I build" with "I am building".

In the context of Racional, this is direct and useful. You say "I oversee our data center projects" for your permanent role, and "Right now, we are building three sites" for what is currently underway. Mastering this difference makes your introduction clear and professional from the very first second of the meeting.
lessons.intro:
Esta segunda é a planta da língua. Você vai aprender a regra que usará na prática de sexta, quando se apresentar a um interlocutor da Microsoft.

Guarde duas frases-âncora: "I oversee our data center projects." (rotina e cargo, Present Simple) e "Right now, we are building three sites." (em andamento, Present Continuous).
lessons.situation: Você prepara a abertura da call mensal com a Microsoft e precisa fixar como falar do seu cargo e do que está em andamento.
lessons.context: Hello, I'm Fábio Viccari. I'm the Director of Operations at Racional. I oversee our data center projects in Brazil. I usually run the monthly review with the client. Right now, we are building three sites and we are hiring two new teams.

vocab.example: I oversee our data center projects.
I am responsible for operations in Brazil.
I report to the CEO.
We are currently building three sites.
I usually meet the client once a month.
The main deliverable is the finished building.
Every stakeholder joins the monthly call.
The schedule is tight this quarter.
The scope includes design and construction.
I handle the relationship with big clients.
The project is on track.
Our headquarters are in São Paulo.
I run the monthly review.
I present the figures every month.
My role is Director of Operations.

exercises.title: 1. Rotina ou agora?
exercises.prompt: Para uma rotina mensal, qual forma é correta? "I ___ the client once a month."

options.whyWrong: O Continuous é para algo acontecendo agora, não para uma rotina.
O '-s' só entra na 3ª pessoa (he/she/it). Com 'I' o verbo fica sem -s.

exercises.title: 2. O que está em andamento
exercises.prompt: Right now, we ___ (build) three sites for Microsoft.
exercises.explanation: 'Right now' pede Present Continuous: are + verbo-ing.

exercises.title: 3. Monte a apresentação
exercises.explanation: Ordem em inglês: sujeito + verbo + objeto. 'I oversee our data center projects.'

exercises.title: 4. Termo e tradução
exercises.explanation: São termos que você usa para descrever seu trabalho e o status das obras.

exercises.title: 5. Sua apresentação em 2 frases
exercises.prompt: Escreva sua apresentação para a call com a Microsoft. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (ex.: role, oversee, schedule, on track). Diga seu cargo e o que está em andamento agora.
exercises.modelAnswer: I'm Fábio, Director of Operations at Racional. I oversee our projects in Brazil. Right now, we are building three sites and the schedule is on track.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos. Mantenha o Present Simple para o cargo e o Continuous para o que está em andamento.

exercises.title: 6. Stative verb
exercises.prompt: Qual é a forma correta? "I ___ the schedule very well."

options.whyWrong: "know" é stative: não usa -ing.
"-s" só na 3ª pessoa (he/she/it).

exercises.title: 7. Terceira pessoa (-s)
exercises.prompt: Racional ___ (build) hospitals, shoppings and data centers.
exercises.explanation: Present Simple, 3ª pessoa do singular (Racional = it): acrescenta -s.

exercises.title: 8. Projeto em andamento agora
exercises.explanation: "Right now" pede Present Continuous: we are delivering a data center right now.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, apresente-se em 15 segundos: diga seu nome, seu cargo na Racional e uma obra que está em andamento agora.
takeaways: I can introduce myself with my name and my role.
I can use the Present Simple for my routine and my job.
I can use the Present Continuous for what is happening now.
I can say what we are building right now.

teacher.overview: Aula de TEORIA conduzida em sala. O aluno NÃO estuda antes: você apresenta a gramática, dá exemplos, deixa ele tentar e volta para breakdowns. Ritmo: explicar → exemplificar com a Racional → o aluno produz → você corrige.
teacher.focus: Estrutura e forma: a regra do dia bem fixada.

flow.how: Leia o overview com ele em voz alta. Pergunte como ele se apresenta hoje. NÃO corrija ainda — colete a base.
Explique no quadro. Peça 2 frases sobre o cargo dele na Racional. Faça breakdown de cada uma.
Contraste com o simple usando a tabela lado a lado. Peça 2 frases sobre o que está em andamento agora nos projetos dele.
Mostre os 3 erros típicos. Dê tempo para ele identificar o erro ANTES de você explicar o porquê.
Faça os exercícios juntos. Para cada erro, pare e explique. Dê tempo; não responda por ele.
Ele fecha com as frases-âncora do cargo. Confirme que ele consegue dizer cargo (simple) + projeto atual (continuous).

watch: Confusão simple/continuous com "right now".
stative verbs com -ing (I am knowing).
esquecer -s na 3ª pessoa (Racional build → builds).
teacher.note: Esta é a aula em que ele ENTENDE a regra. A produção solta fica para a aula de PRÁTICA seguinte — aqui o foco é compreender e fixar com sua ajuda.
teacher.richNote: Esta aula tem conteúdo interativo completo na plataforma (vocabulário, exercícios e recap).

pill.tip: Vogal 'aw' bem aberta: 'coffee' soa como 'CAW-fee' e 'talk' como 'tawk'. Ouça as duas palavras na frase.
pill.sample: I'm gonna grab a coffee, and then we can talk.

grammar.lead: Estes são os dois tempos do presente que você mais usa para se apresentar e abrir reuniões. O Present Simple descreve quem você é e sua rotina (o que é sempre verdade); o Present Continuous descreve o que está em andamento agora. Dominar o contraste entre os dois é a base da sua fala executiva no dia a dia com Microsoft, Amazon e Google.

sections.heading: Present Simple — forma
sections.body: Sujeito + verbo na base. Na 3ª pessoa (he/she/it) acrescenta-se -s. Negativa com do/does + not; pergunta com do/does.

examples.en: I oversee our data center projects in Brazil.
Racional builds hospitals, shopping centers and data centers.
I do not handle procurement; my team does.

sections.heading: Present Simple — usos
sections.body: Para fatos e situações permanentes, rotinas e o seu cargo. É o tempo de "quem eu sou e o que eu faço".

examples.en: I am the Director of Operations at Racional.
We usually run a monthly review with the client.
We are delivering a hyperscale data center right now.
I am preparing the monthly call with Microsoft.

sections.heading: Present Continuous — usos
sections.body: Para o que acontece agora, situações temporárias e projetos em andamento neste ciclo.

examples.en: This quarter we are expanding our data center team.
Right now we are reviewing the project schedule.

sections.heading: Stative verbs — não usam -ing
sections.body: Verbos de estado (opinião, sentido, posse) ficam no Present Simple mesmo quando falamos do agora: know, believe, want, need, mean, understand, have (posse), see, agree. Fonte: British Council.

examples.en: We have three data centers under construction.

contrast.continuous: I am running the review right now.
We are building a data center for the client.
This month I am working from the site.

mistakes.wrong: Look, the client is win the argument.
mistakes.right: Look, the client is winning the argument.

mistakes.wrong: Right now I work on the report.
mistakes.right: Right now I am working on the report.

lessons.title: Self-introduction & seu cargo com interlocutor Microsoft/Amazon/Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você se apresenta e fala do seu cargo em uma conversa real com um interlocutor da Microsoft, Amazon ou Google, sem travar.
lessons.overview:
This is the practice lesson: the construction site that uses Monday's blueprint. Here you do not learn a new rule; you use, out loud and with your teacher, the personal introduction you built with the Present Simple and the Present Continuous. The goal is simple and important: to say who you are with confidence in the first seconds of a meeting with a big data client.

The first contact with Microsoft, Amazon, or Google usually starts with a self-introduction followed by an ice-breaker. You greet the person, say it is a pleasure to meet, comment on the week, and then move to the agenda. It is only a few sentences, but they set the tone of the relationship. An operations director who introduces himself well conveys the solidity of Racional right from the start.

In today's role-play you open the conversation with your counterpart from the client. You will practice safe, ready-made phrases such as "It's a pleasure to meet you" and "Let me walk you through the agenda". The focus is on oral production: speaking, repeating, and gaining fluency with your teacher.
lessons.intro:
Hoje é prática com o professor. Sem teoria nova: você aplica a apresentação de segunda em uma conversa real.

Frases-âncora para a simulação: "It's a pleasure to meet you." · "I'm the Director of Operations at Racional." · "Let me walk you through the agenda."
lessons.situation: Primeira call com seu interlocutor da Microsoft. Vocês se apresentam e você abre a reunião antes de entrar nos números.
lessons.context: Client: Hi Fábio, it's a pleasure to finally meet you. How has your week been? You: Thank you, it's a pleasure to meet you too. My week has been good, thank you. I'm the Director of Operations at Racional, and I take care of our data center projects. Shall we start? Let me walk you through the agenda.

vocab.en: It's a pleasure to meet you
vocab.example: It's a pleasure to meet you.
It's good to finally meet you.
Hi John, how has your week been?
I look forward to this meeting.
On behalf of Racional, welcome.
Let me walk you through the agenda.
I meet my counterpart every month.
We are based in São Paulo.
I take care of our big clients.
Shall we start?
Here is the agenda for today.
Let's kick off the meeting.
I'm glad to be here.
A short question can break the ice.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e digite
exercises.correctText: It's a pleasure to meet you. I'm the Director of Operations at Racional.
exercises.explanation: Frase de abertura padrão: cumprimento + cargo.

exercises.title: 2. Monte a abertura
exercises.explanation: 'Let me walk you through the agenda' = deixe-me apresentar a pauta.

exercises.title: 3. Leia em voz alta
exercises.targetText: It's a pleasure to meet you. I take care of our data center projects. Shall we start?
exercises.translation: É um prazer conhecê-lo. Eu cuido dos nossos projetos de data center. Vamos começar?
exercises.prompt: Você abre a call com seu interlocutor da Microsoft. Diga isso com calma e firmeza.
exercises.explanation: Fale devagar e marque a pausa entre as frases. Essas três frases já abrem qualquer reunião.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, abra uma call de 15 a 20 segundos com a Google: cumprimente, diga seu cargo e convide para começar a pauta, sem ler nenhum texto.
takeaways: I can greet a client and say it's a pleasure to meet them.
I can introduce my role at Racional.
I can open a meeting and walk the client through the agenda.
I can break the ice with a short question.

teacher.overview: Aula de PRÁTICA. NÃO explique gramática nova. Conduza os blocos de produção (drill → role play → conversação → argumentação), dê tempo para ele falar e foque o feedback no contraste simple/continuous e na fluência.
teacher.focus: Fluência aplicada: comunicar sob pressão, sem travar.

flow.how: Relembre as frases-âncora da teoria em 1 minuto. Sem ensinar — só ativar.
Rode o drill 5×, trocando o cliente. Corrija rápido e siga; o objetivo é automatizar.
Faça 2 rodadas. Na 1ª, deixe fluir. Na 2ª, exija um projeto em andamento (continuous) e uma pergunta de retorno.
Anote 3 acertos e 3 erros. Dê feedback ao final, não no meio.
Desafie com 1 pergunta inesperada. Avalie se ele mantém o tempo verbal correto sob pressão.
Resuma 2 pontos fortes e 1 meta para a próxima prática.

watch: Travar e recorrer ao português.
misturar simple/continuous sob pressão.
ler em vez de falar.
teacher.note: Sucesso = ele se apresenta e abre uma call sem ler, com simple para cargo e continuous para o projeto atual.
teacher.richNote: Esta aula tem conteúdo interativo completo na plataforma (vocabulário, exercícios e recap).
teacher.mode: Aula de prática conduzida pelo professor · 1h30 · só produção + feedback

pill.tip: Arrastado (drawl) e o clássico 'y'all' (= you all), com as vogais bem alongadas.
pill.sample: Y'all have a great day now — we'll talk real soon.

practice.lead: Aula de PRÁTICA: sem teoria nova. Você usa, em voz alta e com o professor, o Present Simple e o Present Continuous que viu na teoria. Tudo aqui é produção para receber feedback.
practice.setup: Contexto: primeira call com um interlocutor da Microsoft/Amazon/Google. Você se apresenta, fala do seu cargo e do que está em andamento, e abre a reunião.

blocks.title: Drill — cargo & projeto atual
blocks.prompt: O professor diz um cliente (Microsoft/Amazon/Google) e você responde em 1 frase com Present Simple (cargo) + 1 frase com Present Continuous (projeto agora). Repita 5 vezes, trocando o projeto.
blocks.model: I am the Director of Operations at Racional. Right now we are delivering a data center in Brazil.

blocks.title: Role play — abertura da call
blocks.prompt: Professor é o interlocutor da Microsoft. Cumprimente, apresente-se, diga seu cargo e um projeto em andamento, e convide para começar a pauta — sem ler texto.
blocks.model: It's a pleasure to meet you. I'm Fábio, Director of Operations at Racional. We are currently delivering your data center in Brazil. Shall we start?

blocks.title: Conversação — small talk executivo
blocks.prompt: Troca livre de 2 minutos: o professor pergunta sobre sua semana e seus projetos; responda alternando simple (rotina) e continuous (agora). O professor anota e dá feedback ao final.

blocks.title: Argumentação — por que a Racional
blocks.prompt: Em 60 segundos, defenda por que a Racional é o parceiro certo, usando 2 fatos (simple) e 1 frase de projeto atual (continuous). O professor desafia com 1 pergunta difícil.

blocks.title: Drill — stative verbs
blocks.prompt: O professor diz um verbo de estado (know, want, need, have). Você responde 1 frase no Present Simple sobre a Racional. 6 rodadas.
blocks.model: I know our schedule. We have three projects in progress.

blocks.title: Situação — pergunta inesperada
blocks.prompt: O professor (cliente) pergunta "What are you working on this month?". Responda no Continuous, depois acrescente um fato no Simple.
blocks.model: This month we are finishing your data center. We always deliver on schedule.

blocks.title: Role play — 2ª rodada da call
blocks.prompt: Repita a abertura da call, mas agora o cliente faz 1 pergunta difícil sobre prazo. Mantenha o tempo verbal certo sob pressão.
blocks.model: Right now we are on schedule. We usually finish within 24 months.

blocks.title: Argumentação — sua semana
blocks.prompt: Em 60 segundos, descreva sua semana misturando rotina (Simple) e o que está em andamento (Continuous). O professor dá feedback sobre os dois tempos.

lessons.title: WH-questions, question tags e estruturas de clarificação
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue formar WH-questions, usar question tags simples e pedir esclarecimento de forma educada em inglês.
lessons.overview:
In a meeting with Microsoft, Amazon, or Google, asking good questions is worth as much as giving answers. Whoever asks clearly leads the conversation, confirms what they understood, and avoids misunderstandings about timeline, scope, and cost. For Racional's Operations Director, this is part of the relationship: showing that you listen and that you check every important point.

English organizes information questions with WH-questions (questions with what, when, why, how). The structure is always the same: the WH word comes first, then the auxiliary (do/does/is/are), then the subject and the verb. For example: "When does the project start?". Question tags (short questions at the end, like "right?" or "isn't it?") are used to confirm something in a light way.

When you do not understand, English has ready-made, polite phrases to ask for help: "Could you repeat that?", "Could you slow down?", and "Just to make sure...". Mastering these structures removes the fear of not understanding the client and keeps you in control of the conversation, even with English that is still developing.

lessons.title: Abrindo e conduzindo a primeira reunião — small talk executivo
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue abrir e conduzir a primeira reunião com um cliente, usando small talk executivo e frases para alinhar a pauta.
lessons.overview:
Leading a meeting is more than speaking English: it is guiding the conversation from start to finish. For Racional's Operations Director, opening a call well with Microsoft, Amazon, or Google conveys confidence and organization. A good opening has three simple parts: break the ice, align on the agenda, and start the first point.

The small talk is short and cordial: a question about the trip or the week already creates a connection. Then comes aligning on the agenda: you say what will be covered and check whether the client agrees. Throughout the meeting, you confirm understanding and, at the end, you do the wrap-up with the next steps.

This practice uses the questions and confirmations you studied in the theory lesson. In today's role-play, you lead a meeting from beginning to end with your counterpart from the client, using anchor phrases such as "Let's align on the agenda" and "Let me wrap up with the action items". The focus is on oral production with your teacher.

lessons.title: Números, datas, valores e prazos: a gramática dos numerais em voz alta
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue dizer números grandes, datas, valores e prazos em voz alta, com a gramática correta dos numerais.
lessons.overview:
For an Operations Director, talking about numbers is the heart of the business conversation. In a call with Microsoft, Amazon, or Google, you state contract values, project deadlines, and percentages all the time. Freezing on a large number conveys insecurity; saying "one billion reais" naturally conveys solidity, which is exactly what a construction company with 620 projects needs to communicate.

English has simple rules for this. Large numbers use million and billion with no plural when they come with a number ("two billion", not "two billions"). The decimal point is said as point ("two point five"). Dates use fixed prepositions: by (no later than a certain date) and within (inside a time frame). And a project's duration becomes an adjective: "a 24-month project", with a hyphen and no 's'.

This theory prepares you for Friday's practice, when you will state real values and deadlines from Racional. Here you fix the rule: how to read a value, how to say a percentage with percent, and how to talk about a deadline and a duration. Knowing the correct form before practicing is the safest way to avoid freezing in front of the client.

Esta segunda é a planta da língua: a gramática dos numerais. Você vai usar isso na prática de sexta, falando valores e prazos.

lessons.title: Falando valores de contrato (R$1 bi) e prazos (24 meses) sem travar
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue falar valores de contrato e prazos de obra em voz alta com o cliente, com confiança e sem travar.
lessons.overview:
This practice is the moment to talk real numbers with the client. You have already studied the grammar of numerals in the theory lesson; now you will say, out loud and with your teacher, values like R$ 1 billion and deadlines like 24 months to a counterpart from Microsoft, Amazon, or Google. This is exactly the moment that makes executives freeze the most: the large number right on the tip of the tongue.

In negotiation, the way you say the number counts as much as the number itself. Saying "the investment is in the region of one billion" sounds confident; showing that the project is delivered on schedule or even ahead of schedule conveys Racional's reliability. You also learn to give a rough estimate with ballpark without committing too early.

In today's role-play, you present a contract value and a schedule to the client and answer a question about the timeline. The anchor phrases are short and ready for real use, such as "We commit to deliver within 24 months". The focus is on oral production with your teacher: saying the number without hesitating.

lessons.title: Past Simple vs. Present Perfect: contando a trajetória da empresa
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe quando usar o Past Simple e quando usar o Present Perfect para contar a história e as conquistas da Racional com clareza.
lessons.overview:
Telling a company's story is the foundation of trust. When you talk with a big data client like Microsoft, they want to hear, in a few sentences, how long Racional has existed and what it has already achieved. Racional was founded in 1971; that is more than 50 years of history, 620+ projects, and 10M+ m² built. Knowing how to narrate this is the track record turned into words.

For this, English uses two verb tenses that get mixed up in the mind of a Portuguese speaker. The Past Simple tells a fact with a closed date: "We were founded in 1971." The Present Perfect links the past to the present, with no date: "We have completed over 620 projects." The project is finished, but the number keeps counting today.

This difference is the blueprint of the language for your pitch. Use the Past Simple for the historical milestone (founding, first major project) and the Present Perfect for what has accumulated over the years and still holds true: experience, square meters, segments served. Mastering this rule on Monday gets you ready for Friday's institutional pitch.
lessons.intro:
Duas frases-âncora para você fixar antes da prática: "Racional was founded in 1971." (fato com data, Past Simple) e "We have completed over 620 projects." (resultado que conta até hoje, Present Perfect).

Regra prática: tem ano/data fechada? Past Simple. Quer dizer "até agora", "ao longo dos anos", sem data? Present Perfect com have/has + verbo no particípio.
lessons.situation: Você abre a reunião mensal com a Microsoft e, em poucas frases, conta quando a Racional nasceu e o que ela já entregou.
lessons.context: Racional was founded in 1971. Since then, we have grown a lot. We have completed over 620 projects and we have built more than 10 million square meters. Over the years, we have delivered hospitals, malls and data centers. We started small, but today we are a strong company.

lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue entregar, com o professor, o pitch institucional "Racional in 3 minutes", apresentando os pontos fortes da empresa para um cliente Microsoft.
lessons.overview:
The institutional pitch is the first major moment of trust with a big data client. In three minutes, you need to say who Racional is, how long it has existed, and why it is a strong partner. It is not a technical engineering speech: it is a business talk, calm and organized, that shows solidity. The Microsoft client only pays attention to numbers after understanding who they are talking to.

This Friday you do not learn new grammar. You return to Monday's structure — was founded for the date and we have delivered for the results — and use it in a speaking simulation. The goal is to chain three blocks together: the track record (50+ years, 620+ projects), what the company does, and why it stands out.

The scenario is a call with Microsoft's new infrastructure director, who asked for a quick overview of the company. You will practice the opening (to give you a quick overview), the body, and the closing (to wrap up). The weight of the lesson is on oral production with your teacher, not on writing.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora para a simulação: "Let me give you a quick overview of Racional." / "We were founded in 1971, and since then we have completed over 620 projects." / "In a nutshell, we are a strong and reliable partner."

Use estas três frases como abertura, corpo e fechamento do seu pitch de 3 minutos.

lessons.title: Linguagem de solidez: adjetivos, intensificadores e collocations
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você domina a linguagem de solidez — adjetivos, intensificadores e collocations — para descrever a Racional sem soar exagerado.
lessons.overview:
For a big data client, the most important word is not "big": it is solid. Microsoft, Amazon, and Google choose partners that convey security. That is why the language of solidity is a business tool: the right adjectives make the client feel that Racional is reliable even before seeing a number. This is Pillar 1 of your program — building trust.

In this lesson you learn three pieces. First, the adjectives of solidity: solid, robust, reliable. Second, intensifiers, which add strength without exaggeration: highly, extremely. Third, collocations — fixed combinations that sound natural: a proven track record, robust financials, a solid reputation.

The rule is simple and it is Friday's blueprint: the intensifier comes before the adjective ("highly reliable") and collocations should be used whole, as blocks. Applied to Racional, this means saying "We are a well-established company with robust financials" — a sentence that inspires confidence at Amazon without a single difficult word.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "We are a solid and reliable company." / "We have a proven track record." / "Our financials are robust."

Lembre: o intensificador (highly, extremely) vem antes do adjetivo, e as collocations (proven track record, robust financials) são usadas como blocos inteiros.
lessons.situation: Você prepara, em voz alta, as frases de solidez que dirá na próxima reunião — quer que a Amazon ouça robustez sem você soar exagerado.
lessons.context: Racional is a solid and reliable company. We are well-established in Brazil. We have a proven track record and a solid reputation. Our financials are robust. We are highly experienced in large projects. This makes us a trustworthy partner for you.

lessons.title: Apresentando solidez e robustez financeira a um cliente Amazon/AWS
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue apresentar, com o professor, a solidez e a robustez financeira da Racional a um cliente Amazon/AWS que questiona a saúde financeira da empresa.
lessons.overview:
In large, long projects, like an Amazon/AWS data center, the client always asks: "do you have the financial strength to sustain this to the end?". It is a fair question, and answering it well is part of the negotiation. The client wants peace of mind: knowing that the project will not stop halfway through for lack of money.

This Friday you return to Monday's language of solidity and apply it to a real situation under pressure. The structure to use is to reassure with facts: acknowledge the question as legitimate, show the company's financial strength and stability, and promise delivery from start to finish.

The scenario is a meeting with the account manager from Amazon/AWS. He asks directly whether Racional can take on a long-term project. You will practice the answer that reassures the client without sounding defensive: Racional has the solidity to honor commitments, and the client can count on it. The focus is on oral production with your teacher.

Frases-âncora para a simulação: "That's a fair question." / "We have the financial strength to take on long-term projects." / "You can count on us from start to finish."

lessons.title: Relative clauses para descrever segmentos e serviços
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa relative clauses (with who, which, that, where) para descrever, em uma só frase elegante, os segmentos e serviços da Racional.
lessons.overview:
When you present Racional's segments — healthcare, shopping centers, industry, and data centers — you can say it all in short, separate sentences, or you can combine the information into a single, more sophisticated sentence. The tool that does this is the relative clause. For a Google client, describing a segment precisely shows that Racional understands their sector.

The rule is this lesson's blueprint. Use which or that for things ("a segment that requires precision"), who for people ("the teams who run the site"), and where for places ("a hospital where safety is critical"). The relative clause comes right after the noun it describes, without repeating that noun.

Applied to Racional, this allows rich yet simple sentences: "We build data centers, which require high precision" or "We serve the healthcare segment, where safety is essential." Each segment (healthcare, retail, industrial facility) gets a clear description that prepares you for Friday's role-play with Google.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora: "We build data centers, which require high precision." / "We serve the healthcare segment, where safety is critical." / "We work with clients who demand quality."

Lembre: which/that para coisas, who para pessoas, where para lugares. A oração relativa vem logo depois do substantivo.

lessons.context: Racional works in many segments. We build data centers, which require high precision. We serve the healthcare segment, where safety is critical. We also build malls, which welcome thousands of people. We work with clients who demand quality. Every segment needs a tailored solution.

lessons.title: Os segmentos da Racional (saúde, shopping, indústria, data center)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue apresentar, com o professor, os quatro segmentos da Racional a um cliente Google e conectar a fala ao projeto do cliente.
lessons.overview:
Showing the portfolio of segments is the way to prove that Racional is not a company of just one type of project. Healthcare, shopping centers, industry, and hyperscale data centers: each one requires different solutions, and Racional operates in all of them. For a Google client, seeing this variety conveys expertise and shows that the company is versatile.

This Friday you return to Monday's relative clauses and use them in a real portfolio presentation. The structure is: list the segments, describe each one with a short sentence, and, at the end, connect everything to the client's project — saying that Racional is no stranger to hyperscale projects and that it understands a project like yours.

The scenario is a relationship meeting with Google. You present the four segments and steer the conversation toward the client's hyperscale data center. You will practice the speech that shows Racional can tailor the solution to Google's need. The weight of the lesson is on the role-play and on speaking out loud with your teacher.

lessons.title: Voz passiva: descrevendo obras entregues e processos de execução
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe usar a voz passiva no presente e no passado para descrever obras entregues e processos de execução da Racional.
lessons.overview:
When an operations director presents Racional, he needs to talk about the projects the company has already delivered. The most important thing is not to say who did it, but to show what was built, delivered, and completed. That is more than 620 projects and 10 million square meters over more than 50 years. This track record is what builds trust with clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google.

To describe this kind of result, English makes heavy use of the passive voice. Instead of "we built the hospital", the focus shifts to the project: "the hospital was built". This sounds more technical and executive, and it is exactly how engineers describe deliveries: the project was designed, executed, inspected, and delivered. The subject of the sentence becomes the project, not the team.

This theory lesson is the blueprint of the language for Friday's practice, when you will present Racional's cases. Here you learn the rule calmly: the formula to be + past participle and where the verb tense lives. Think of it like engineering: first the structure, then the application on site.
lessons.intro:
A regra é mecânica: to be + past participle. O tempo verbal mora sempre no "to be".

Presente (processo de hoje): "The data center is designed for big data."
Passado (obra concluída): "The hospital was built in 2019."
Para escolher o tempo, decida só "is/are" (agora) ou "was/were" (antes) e mantenha o particípio fixo: built, delivered, completed, designed, awarded.
lessons.situation: Você prepara, com calma, as frases que vai usar numa call com a Microsoft para descrever duas obras de referência da Racional.
lessons.context: The Einstein hospital was built in 2019. It was delivered on time and on budget. Today, each data center is designed for big clients. Every site is inspected every week. The contract was awarded to Racional after a long process.

vocab.example: The hospital was built in 2019.
The project was delivered on time.
The first phase is completed.
The center is designed for big data.
The contract was awarded to us.
The building is commissioned by our team.
The site is delivered turnkey.
"Built" is the past participle of "build".
The work was carried out safely.
The building was handed over to the client.
Einstein is a reference project.
We have a strong track record.
It has ten thousand square meters.
It was delivered on time and on budget.

exercises.title: 1. Onde mora o tempo verbal?
exercises.prompt: Você quer dizer que o hospital FOI construído em 2019 (passado). Qual frase está correta?

options.whyWrong: "Is" é presente. Para um fato de 2019 (passado), o "to be" vai para o passado: "was built".
Depois de "was" vem o particípio "built", não o verbo base "build".

exercises.title: 2. Processo de hoje (presente passivo)
exercises.prompt: Cada data center é projetado para clientes grandes: "Each data center ___ (design) for big clients."
exercises.explanation: Processo atual e geral = presente passivo: is + particípio (designed).

commonErrors.designs: "Designs" é voz ativa. Aqui o foco é o data center recebendo a ação: "is designed".
commonErrors.was designed: "Was" é passado. Para um processo atual use o presente: "is designed".

exercises.title: 3. Monte a frase da obra entregue
exercises.explanation: Sujeito (The project) + to be no passado (was) + particípio (delivered) + complemento (on time).

exercises.title: 4. Combine o verbo com o particípio
exercises.explanation: Verbos regulares ganham -ed. "Build" é irregular: built. Decore os irregulares que você mais usa.

exercises.title: 5. Descreva uma obra entregue (2 frases)
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases na voz passiva sobre uma obra da Racional para apresentar à Amazon: (1) o que foi entregue e quando; (2) um detalhe do processo no presente. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta lição. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
keywords: was built|was delivered|was completed|was handed over|was awarded
exercises.modelAnswer: The Einstein hospital was delivered in 2019, on time and on budget. Today each new project is designed for big clients.
exercises.explanation: Uma frase no passado (obra concluída) + uma no presente (processo padrão) = portfólio descrito com autoridade.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, descreva uma obra real da Racional usando voz passiva: o que foi entregue, quando e como é executado hoje. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can describe a finished project with the passive voice (was built, was delivered).
I can describe a process in the present passive (is designed, is inspected).
I know the time sits in the verb "to be", so I stop mixing past and present.
I can present Racional's track record in a simple and clear way.

lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta, em conversação com a Microsoft, os cases e o portfólio da Racional usando a voz passiva e números fortes.
lessons.overview:
A case study is the strongest way to show competence. Instead of adjectives, you show real projects: the Einstein hospital, the Sirius accelerator, the Arena MRV, and the data centers of clients like Itaú and Vivo. This is Racional's portfolio, and it speaks for itself: it speaks for itself.

For an operations director, citing a flagship project shows the client that the company has already been trusted with projects of high complexity. Microsoft, Amazon, and Google want to know whether you have already delivered large, modern data centers. A good case answers that with facts and numbers, without exaggeration.

This is Friday's practice lesson. No new theory: you return to Monday's passive voice and practice the speech with your teacher. The structure of a case in three sentences is simple: (1) what and when, (2) the number that impresses, (3) what this proves. The weight here is on oral production.
lessons.intro:
Use estas três frases-âncora na simulação:

1) "The Sirius project was delivered in 2018."
2) "It has 68,000 square meters."
3) "This shows we can handle complex projects."

lessons.title: Marcadores temporais e sequência (since, by, until, over the years)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa marcadores de tempo (since, for, by, until, over the years) com o Present Perfect para contar a história e o crescimento da Racional.
lessons.overview:
Racional was founded in 1971. That is more than 50 years of history, and telling this story is a strong way to show solidity to Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. For this, English uses time markers: since, for, over the years, and to date. They link the past to the present.

The grammar point of this lesson is the Present Perfect (have/has + past participle). It is used for something that started in the past and continues today: "Racional has grown since 1971." For the engineer, the rule is clear: use since with a point in time (since 1971) and for with a duration (for 50 years). It is the structure that describes a milestone or a track record that is still alive.

This is Monday's theory lesson. Here you learn the rule calmly, with examples connected to Racional's history. On Friday, this becomes the narrative you tell the client. First the structure, then the project.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora para a prática:

"Racional has built projects since 1971."
"We have grown a lot over the years."
Regra: since + ponto no tempo (since 1971); for + duração (for 50 years).
lessons.situation: Você prepara as frases para abrir uma reunião com o Google contando, de forma curta, a história e o crescimento da Racional.
lessons.context: Racional was founded in 1971. We have built projects since then. For more than fifty years, we have grown a lot. Over the years, we have worked in many sectors. To date, we have completed more than 620 projects.

vocab.example: We have worked here since 1971.
We have grown for fifty years.
The work will be ready by June.
We worked until late.
We have changed a lot over the years.
Racional was founded in 1971.
We have grown for many decades.
This project was a big milestone.
We grew into a big company.
We expanded into data centers.
We have grown ever since.
To date, we have built 620 projects.
We work throughout Brazil.
"We have built" is Present Perfect.

exercises.title: 1. Since ou for?
exercises.prompt: Você quer dizer que a Racional cresce DESDE 1971. Qual frase está correta?

options.whyWrong: "For" é usado com duração (for 50 years), não com um ano. Com um ano use "since".
Com "since" e história até hoje, use Present Perfect: "have grown", não o presente simples.

exercises.title: 2. Quanto tempo? (for)
exercises.prompt: São mais de 50 anos de história: "Racional has worked here ___ more than fifty years."
exercises.explanation: "For" + duração (fifty years). "Since" seria com um ponto no tempo (since 1971).

commonErrors.since: "Since" precisa de um ponto no tempo (since 1971). Com uma duração (fifty years) use "for".
commonErrors.during: "During" pede um evento (during the project), não um número de anos. Use "for".

exercises.title: 3. Monte a frase da história
exercises.explanation: Present Perfect (have worked) + complemento + marcador de tempo (over the years) no fim.

exercises.title: 4. Combine o marcador com o seu uso
exercises.explanation: Cada marcador tem uma função. "Since" e "for" combinam com o Present Perfect.

exercises.title: 5. Conte a história em 2 frases
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases sobre a história da Racional para abrir uma reunião com o Google. Use Present Perfect e ao menos 2 marcadores de tempo desta lição (ex.: since, for, over the years, to date). A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
keywords: have built|have grown|have worked|have completed|was founded
exercises.modelAnswer: Racional was founded in 1971. Since then, we have grown a lot and, to date, we have completed more than 620 projects.
exercises.explanation: Fundação no passado + crescimento até hoje com Present Perfect = história contada com solidez.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, conte a história da Racional desde 1971 até hoje em poucas frases, usando since, for e over the years. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can say when Racional was founded.
I can use "since" with a year and "for" with a duration.
I can use the Present Perfect to connect the past to today.
I can tell the company history in a short and clear way.

lessons.title: Storytelling: das ondas do mercado ao ciclo atual de cloud/IA
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conta, em conversação, a trajetória da Racional pelas ondas do mercado até o ciclo atual de cloud e IA, num storytelling para clientes big data.
lessons.overview:
Every strong company has a story of change. Racional went through several market waves: hospitals, shopping centers, industry, and now data centers for cloud and AI. Knowing how to tell a story of these waves shows the client that the company knows how to read the market and adapt.

For an operations director, the key point is the turning point: the moment when Racional decided to shift toward data centers. Today there is strong demand for cloud infrastructure in Brazil, coming from Microsoft, Amazon, and Google. The message is simple: the company is well positioned for the next chapter.

This is Friday's practice lesson. No new theory: you use the verb tenses you have already seen (past simple and Present Perfect) and practice the narrative with your teacher. The structure is "at first... then... looking ahead". The weight is on speaking.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora para a simulação:

"At first, we built hospitals and malls."
"Then, we started to shift toward data centers."
"Looking ahead, we are well placed for cloud and AI."
lessons.situation: Numa conversa com a Amazon, você conta de forma curta como a Racional chegou ao ciclo atual de data centers para cloud e IA.
lessons.context: Let me tell you our story. At first, we built hospitals and malls. Then, we started to shift toward data centers. There is strong demand for cloud in Brazil now. This was a turning point for us. Looking ahead, we are well placed for the next chapter.

vocab.example: Let me tell you a short story.

There is strong demand for data centers.
We are well placed for the future.

exercises.explanation: Ouça e escreva. Note os conectores "at first" e "then", que organizam a história.

exercises.explanation: "Looking ahead" abre a frase do futuro: "we are well placed for cloud".

exercises.explanation: Começo, virada e futuro em três passos. Repita até a narrativa sair natural.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta e sem texto, conte para o Google a trajetória da Racional: como começou, qual foi o ponto de virada para data centers e por que está bem posicionada para cloud e IA. Cerca de 15 a 20 segundos.
takeaways: I can tell our company story with "at first", "then" and "looking ahead".

lessons.title: Modelo de negócio: viability → engineering → pre-construction → build
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve o modelo de negócio da Racional em etapas (viability, engineering, pre-construction, build) usando conectores de sequência.
lessons.overview:
Racional's business model follows four stages: viability, engineering, pre-construction, and build. Explaining this path step-by-step shows the client that the company has a clear method, not improvisation. For an engineer, this is the natural way to think: first the blueprint, then the project.

The grammar point of this lesson is the sequence connectors: first, next, after that, and finally. They order the stages and make the explanation easy to follow. The rule is simple: a connector opens each stage, in the right order, and the client follows the reasoning without getting lost.

This is Monday's theory lesson. Here you learn the rule and the vocabulary of the stages calmly. On Friday, this becomes the explanation you give Google about how Racional delivers a project from start to finish. First the structure, then the application.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora para a prática:

"First, we assess viability."
"Next, we do the engineering."
"After that, we plan the pre-construction."
"Finally, we build and hand over."
lessons.situation: Você prepara as frases para explicar ao Google, passo a passo, como a Racional conduz um projeto da viabilidade até a entrega.
lessons.context: Let me explain our model step by step. First, we assess viability. Next, we do the engineering. After that, we plan the pre-construction. Finally, we build the project and hand it over to the client.

vocab.example: We have four stages.
Let me explain step by step.
First we check the viability.
We assess the project first.
Next we do the engineering.
Pre-construction comes before the build.
Finally we build the project.
First, we assess viability.
Next, we do the engineering.
After that, we plan the work.
Finally, we hand it over.
We move from design to build.
This is our approach.
We hand over the building to the client.

exercises.title: 1. Qual conector abre a primeira etapa?
exercises.prompt: Você quer dizer que a PRIMEIRA etapa é avaliar a viabilidade. Qual frase está correta?

options.whyWrong: "Finally" é a última etapa. A primeira etapa começa com "first".
"After that" vem depois de outra etapa. Para a primeira, use "first".

exercises.title: 2. A última etapa (finally)
exercises.prompt: A última etapa é construir e entregar: "___, we build the project and hand it over."
exercises.explanation: "Finally" abre a última etapa da sequência.

commonErrors.First: "First" é a primeira etapa. Aqui é a última, então use "Finally".
commonErrors.Next: "Next" é uma etapa do meio. Para a última use "Finally".

exercises.title: 3. Monte a etapa de engenharia
exercises.explanation: Conector (Next) + sujeito (we) + verbo (do) + complemento (the engineering).

exercises.title: 4. Combine a etapa com a sua ordem
exercises.explanation: As quatro etapas seguem sempre a mesma ordem. Cada conector marca o lugar de cada uma.

exercises.title: 5. Explique o modelo em 2 ou 3 frases
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 ou 3 frases explicando, passo a passo, o modelo da Racional para o Google. Use ao menos 2 conectores de sequência desta lição (first, next, after that, finally) e os nomes das etapas. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: Let me explain step by step. First, we assess viability. Next, we do the engineering. Finally, we build the project and hand it over.
exercises.explanation: Conectores em ordem + nomes das etapas = um método claro e fácil de seguir.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, explique o modelo de negócio da Racional em quatro etapas, usando first, next, after that e finally. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can name the four stages of our model.
I can use "first", "next", "after that" and "finally" in order.
I can explain our approach step by step.
I can say that we build the project and hand it over to the client.

lessons.title: Apresentando o diferencial de pré-construção e PMG ao Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta, em conversação com o Google, o diferencial de pré-construção e governança (PMG) da Racional, ligando cada ponto a um benefício para o cliente.
lessons.overview:
Racional's main differentiator is its strong pre-construction and its project governance (PMG). Planning in detail before starting construction is what sets us apart. For clients like Google, who need data centers delivered without surprises, this care makes all the difference.

For an operations director, the central message is risk reduction: to plan in detail makes the project more predictable, with fewer surprises. This is added value and gives the client peace of mind. The good practice is to always link the differentiator to a benefit: "this means... / as a result... / this matters because...".

This is Friday's practice lesson. No new theory: you return to the structures from the previous lessons and practice, with your teacher, the sales talk about the differentiator. The weight is on oral production, linking each technical point to what it means for the client.

"We plan in detail. As a result, the project is more predictable."
"This matters because it gives you fewer surprises."

lessons.title: Modais de polidez (would, could, may) e hedging; registro formal
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você saberá usar os modais de polidez (would, could, may) e palavras de hedging para fazer pedidos e sugestões soarem corteses no registro formal.
lessons.overview:
In a long-term relationship with clients like Microsoft, Amazon, and Google, register (the level of formality) is a business tool. In a monthly meeting on a large contract, the way you ask is worth as much as what you ask. A request that is too direct can sound like an order; a courteous request opens space for trust to grow. That is why this module works on a formal yet close tone — firm without being rude.

This lesson is the blueprint of the language: before Friday's practice, you study the rule for politeness modals. Would you like…? turns a request into an invitation. Could you…? asks with elegance. May I suggest…? is the most formal and is used to propose a path without imposing it. As an operations director, you use these forms to lead the room without ever seeming to give orders to the client.

The second resource is hedging (softening your speech): small cushions such as perhaps, it might be worth…, and I would say…. They soften an opinion without weakening it. The golden rule: the larger the contract and the newer the relationship, the more you swap the direct verb for a modal and add a cushion. This is the foundation you will apply on Friday, in the first meeting with a new director from Microsoft.
lessons.intro:
A regra é simples: para pedir, use Could you…?; para oferecer ou convidar, use Would you like…?; para propor um caminho, use May I suggest…?. Todos vêm seguidos do verbo no infinitivo sem "to" (Could you send…?), exceto "Would you like", que pede "to" (Would you like to start…?).

Para suavizar opiniões, acrescente uma almofada de hedging: "Perhaps we could review the plan" ou "I would say the schedule is tight." Guarde estas três frases-âncora para a prática: "Would you like to begin?", "Could you share the figures?" e "May I suggest we align on priorities?"
lessons.situation: Você está preparando o tom da primeira reunião mensal com um novo diretor da Microsoft. O registro precisa ser formal e cortês, sem soar submisso.
lessons.context: Good morning. Thank you for making the time. Would you like to begin with the schedule? Could you share the latest figures with us? May I suggest we align on priorities first? I would say the plan is solid, but perhaps it might be worth checking the contract scope again.

lessons.title: Primeiro contato de relacionamento com novo interlocutor da Microsoft
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduzirá, em conversação com o professor, o primeiro contato com um novo interlocutor da Microsoft, aplicando os modais de polidez e o hedging da aula de teoria.
lessons.overview:
Every long-term relationship has a first meeting, and it carries a lot of weight. When a new account director at Microsoft inherits the account from Racional, he still does not know whether he can trust you. The first 90 seconds are the moment to set the tone: warm, respectful, and confident. This is where a partnership of many years either starts well or starts cold.

This lesson is Monday's project on site. You do not study new grammar: you apply the politeness modals and hedging in a real conversation with your teacher. The script has four moves: thank the person and break the ice ("Thank you for making the time"), introduce yourself and Racional, offer control of the agenda with a modal ("Would you like to start with…?"), and make yourself available ("My team is at your disposal"). You are the host, and whoever leads with courtesy controls the room.

As an operations director, you do this often: the large accounts at Microsoft, Amazon, and Google change their contact person, and each new point of contact needs to feel, right from the start, that Racional is a trusted partner. Today's goal is to build rapport before talking about numbers, making the person comfortable to work with you going forward.
lessons.intro: Leve estas frases-âncora para a simulação: "Welcome on board. Thank you for making the time." para abrir; "I'll be your main point of contact, and my team is at your disposal." para se posicionar; e "Would you like a quick overview first?" para passar o controle da pauta com cortesia.
lessons.situation: Primeira call com a nova diretora de conta da Microsoft, que acaba de herdar o relacionamento com a Racional. Os 90 segundos iniciais definem se ela confia em você.
lessons.context: Good morning, and welcome on board. Thank you for making the time to meet us. I am Fábio, Director of Operations at Racional. It is a real pleasure to start working with you. I will be your main point of contact, and my team is at your disposal. Would you like a quick overview of the partnership first?

lessons.title: Present perfect continuous para histórico de parceria
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você saberá usar o present perfect continuous (have been working) para falar do histórico de uma parceria que começou no passado e continua até hoje.
lessons.overview:
Racional's greatest asset with clients like Microsoft, Amazon and Google is time: decades of projects delivered and a solid track record. For an operations director, knowing how to tell that history in English is a relationship weapon. It is not enough to say "we worked together"; you have to show that the partnership is long-standing and that trust was built steadily over the years.

This is today's language blueprint: the present perfect continuous. It connects past and present to show an action that started before and keeps happening. The form is simple: have/has + been + verb-ing. "We have been working with you for ten years" says the partnership started ten years ago and is still alive today. This is exactly the idea of an ongoing relationship that you want to convey to the client.

You will pair this verb tense with two key words: since, for the starting point (since 2010), and for, for the duration (for a decade). In Friday's practice, you will use this structure to show Microsoft that Racional has been building trust and strengthening the partnership year after year. Today, the focus is mastering the rule before stepping onto the site.
lessons.intro:
A regra-âncora: have/has + been + verbo-ing. Use since para o início ("since 2010") e for para a duração ("for a decade"). Guarde estas frases para a prática: "We have been working with you since 2010" e "We have been building trust for over a decade."

Cuidado: "for" pede um período (for ten years); "since" pede um ponto no tempo (since 2010).
lessons.situation: Numa reunião mensal com o Google, você quer abrir lembrando há quanto tempo a Racional vem entregando e fortalecendo a parceria.
lessons.context: We have been working with the Google team since 2010. We have been building trust steadily, year after year. It is a long-standing partnership, and the relationship keeps growing. We have been delivering for you for over a decade, and our goal is to strengthen it even more.

Our partnership is strong and stable.

We build trust with every project.

lessons.title: "We've been delivering for you since…" — relacionamento de longevidade
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você dirá, em conversação com o professor, há quanto tempo a Racional vem entregando para o cliente, usando o histórico da parceria como argumento de relacionamento.
lessons.overview:
When a contract reaches renewal time, the past speaks loudly. Saying "We've been delivering for you since…" is not just a date: it is living proof that Racional is reliable and that the client can count on the company. For Microsoft, Amazon and Google, longevity is security — and security is what you are selling.

This lesson is Friday's site work. No new grammar: you apply the present perfect continuous from lesson 21 in a contract renewal role-play. The scenario sets up a conversation in which the client is thinking about renewing, and you use the history to show consistency: milestones met, promises delivered, years side by side. The goal is to look back in order to open up the future.

As an operations director, this is how you defend a renewal or a scope expansion. You remind the client that Racional has been standing by them, that every milestone was met, and that trust was earned through proven work. Today, the weight is on speaking: you will train these sentences out loud with the teacher.
lessons.intro: Frases-âncora para a simulação: "We have been delivering for you since 2010, and we have met every milestone." para abrir com histórico; "You can count on us — we are a reliable partner." para reforçar a confiança; e "We are proud to look back and proud to renew." para fechar pedindo a renovação.
lessons.situation: Reunião de renovação de contrato com a Amazon. O cliente pensa em renovar, e você usa o histórico de entregas da Racional para mostrar que pode contar com a empresa.
lessons.context: We have been delivering for you since 2010. In all these years, we have met every milestone, on time and side by side with your team. You can count on us. We are a reliable partner, and the trust between us is proven. We would be proud to renew the contract and keep standing by you.

lessons.title: will vs. going to: promises & commitments
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você saberá usar 'will' e 'going to' para fazer promessas e assumir compromissos de forma clara com o cliente.
lessons.overview:
In a large contract with Microsoft, Amazon or Google, the operations director's word is worth gold. Making a commitment clearly in English is part of the long-term relationship: the client needs to know exactly what you guarantee and what is going to happen. That is why this lesson works on the language of promises and commitment, always tied to delivery, deadlines and compliance.

This is today's language blueprint: the difference between will and going to. Use will for a promise or a decision made on the spot: "I will make sure the team is ready" (I guarantee it). Use going to for a plan already decided: "We are going to follow the safety protocol" (it is already agreed). Both talk about the future, but with different intentions: will is a personal commitment; going to is a firm plan.

You will pair this rule with commitment expressions: to commit to, to guarantee, to give my word and rest assured. In Friday's practice, you will use all of this to reassure the client that Racional stands behind every stage. Today, the focus is understanding when to use each form before applying it.
lessons.intro:
A regra-âncora: will = promessa/decisão na hora ("I will make sure…"); going to = plano já decidido ("We are going to follow the protocol"). Os dois vêm seguidos do verbo no infinitivo sem 'to' depois de 'will', e com 'going to' + verbo.

Guarde estas frases: "I will make sure the team is ready.", "We are going to follow the safety protocol." e "Rest assured, we will deal with it at every stage."
lessons.situation: Numa reunião com a Microsoft, o cliente está preocupado com prazo e segurança. Você precisa assumir compromissos claros para tranquilizá-lo.
lessons.context: I understand your concern, and I will deal with it personally. I will make sure the team is ready on time. We are going to follow the safety protocol at every stage. I give you my word: we commit to full compliance. Rest assured, Racional stands behind every promise we make.

vocab.example: I will make sure the team is ready.
We are going to follow the protocol.
We commit to full compliance.
Our commitment is clear.
We guarantee the deadline.
I give you my word.
I will deal with the issue today.
We follow the safety protocol.
Compliance protects everyone on site.
Let me address your concern.
We check quality at every stage.
Rest assured, we will be on time.
We stand behind our work.

I can describe a firm plan with 'going to'.

lessons.title: Demonstrando capacidade de entrega e compromisso (24 meses)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresentará, em conversação com o professor, a capacidade de entrega da Racional para um projeto de 24 meses, mostrando compromisso etapa por etapa.
lessons.overview:
A data center for Microsoft or Amazon is a project of many months, divided into phases. The client wants the confidence that Racional has the delivery capacity to sustain 24 months of work on time and on budget. Showing this in English, in a calm and structured way, is what separates a supplier from a long-term partner.

This lesson is Friday's site work. No new grammar: you apply 'will' and 'going to' from lesson 23 in a role-play where you present the execution plan for a 24-month project. The scenario asks you to break the project down stage by stage, explain each phase and promise to keep the client posted. The structure reassures as much as the content.

As an operations director, you use this speech to take control of the project without arrogance: "We are going to oversee every milestone", "You have my word", "We take ownership". Today the weight is on speaking: you will train with the teacher the firm and organized tone of someone who delivers without compromising quality.
lessons.intro: Frases-âncora para a simulação: "We are going to break the project into phases and oversee every milestone." para mostrar método; "We will deliver on time and on budget, without compromise." para o compromisso; e "You have my word — we take full ownership." para fechar com responsabilidade.
lessons.situation: Apresentação à Microsoft do plano de execução de um data center de 24 meses. Você mostra que a Racional tem capacidade de entregar etapa por etapa, no prazo e no orçamento.
lessons.context: This is a 24-month project, and we have a robust plan. We are going to break it into phases and oversee every milestone, stage by stage. We will deliver on time and on budget, without compromise. We will keep you posted at every step. You have my word: we take full ownership of the delivery.

lessons.title: Linkers de causa/consequência e contextualização
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conecta causa e consequência com clareza e dá o contexto antes de expor um fato, usando linkers como 'because', 'due to', 'so', 'therefore' e 'that's why'.
lessons.overview:
A project director does not drop the news first: he explains the background and then presents the fact. In building large data centers for Microsoft, Amazon and Google, almost everything connects through a chain of cause and effect: a steel delay, heavy rain, a change in scope. Whoever can link these pieces in English conveys control; whoever just announces the change seems to be losing command of the project.

The heart of this lesson is the linkers (connectors). They fall into two groups. The cause ones answer the why: because, since, due to. The consequence ones show the result: so, therefore, as a result and that's why. There is a precise rule worth fixing here: after 'because' comes a full sentence, and after 'due to' comes only a noun.

For Fábio, this structure is the basis of the monthly meetings with the big data clients. Before saying "we adjusted the schedule", the professional path is: to give context, point to the root cause and measure the impact. This is the language blueprint; on Friday you raise the structure in a real conversation with the client.
lessons.intro:
Guarde duas frases-âncora para a prática: "Let me give you some context first." e "The supply chain was tight, so we added a buffer."

E grave a regra de ouro da estrutura: because + frase completa (because the schedule was tight); due to + substantivo (due to a port issue). Causa primeiro, consequência depois.
lessons.situation: Numa reunião mensal com a Microsoft, você precisa explicar por que ajustou a fase estrutural. Em vez de só anunciar a mudança, você dá o contexto antes.
lessons.context: Let me give you some context first. The steel delivery was late due to a port problem. Because we planned a buffer from the start, the final date does not change. The impact on the timeline is very small, so we are still on schedule.

vocab.pt: porque (introduz a causa, com frase completa)
vocab.example: We changed the plan because the schedule was tight.

vocab.pt: devido a (introduz a causa, com substantivo)
vocab.example: The delay happened due to a port problem.
Since the budget is fixed, we kept the scope small.
The supply chain was tight, so we added a buffer.
Costs went up, and as a result we checked the estimate again.
The risk is low. Therefore, we can commit to the date.
Safety comes first, and that's why we check the site every week.
Let me give you some context first.
The reason is a change in the local rules.
The early decision led to a faster delivery.
Good planning results in fewer surprises.
The impact on the timeline was very small.
We found the root cause very fast.
Let me share some background before the numbers.

exercises.title: 1. Causa com frase ou com substantivo?
exercises.prompt: Você quer dizer "devido a um problema no porto". Qual forma está correta?

options.whyWrong: Depois de 'because' vem uma frase completa (sujeito + verbo), não um substantivo solto. Diga 'due to a port problem' ou 'because there was a port problem'.

options.text: due to a port problem happened
options.whyWrong: Depois de 'due to' vem só o substantivo, sem verbo. O 'happened' sobra aqui.

exercises.explanation: 'Because' + frase completa. 'Due to' + substantivo. Essa é a regra que mais trava brasileiros.

exercises.title: 2. Marque a consequência
exercises.prompt: The supply chain was tight, ___ we added a two-month buffer.
exercises.explanation: 'So' liga a causa à consequência: causa primeiro, resultado depois. 'Therefore' e 'as a result' são variantes mais formais.

commonErrors.because: 'Because' introduz a causa, não a consequência. Aqui o que vem depois é o resultado.
commonErrors.due to: 'Due to' introduz causa com substantivo, não conecta dois resultados.

exercises.title: 3. Contexto antes da decisão
exercises.explanation: Começar pela causa ('Because the schedule was tight,') prepara o cliente para a decisão que vem depois. Contexto primeiro, sempre.

exercises.title: 4. Combine o linker com a função

pairs.left: let me give you some context
pairs.right: abre a explicação antes do fato

exercises.explanation: Cada linker tem uma função fixa. Saber qual usa frase e qual usa substantivo evita o erro mais comum.

exercises.title: 5. Explique uma decisão com contexto (2 frases)
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases para a Microsoft explicando uma decisão de cronograma: (1) dê a causa/contexto e (2) apresente a consequência. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta lição. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
keywords: so|therefore|as a result|that's why|led to|resulted in
exercises.modelAnswer: Let me give you some context first. The steel delivery was late due to a port problem. Because we planned a buffer, the final date does not change, so we are still on schedule.
exercises.explanation: Contexto (causa) + decisão (consequência) = o cliente entende o seu raciocínio e confia na sua gestão.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em 15 segundos, explique uma decisão recente do seu projeto começando pela causa e terminando na consequência. Use 'because' (ou 'due to') e depois 'so'. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can introduce a cause with 'because' plus a full sentence.
I can introduce a cause with 'due to' plus a noun.
I can mark a consequence with 'so', 'therefore' or 'as a result'.
I can give context before I state a decision.
