lessons.title: Contextualizar antes de expor: explicando o "porquê" ao cliente
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você contextualiza antes de expor numa conversa real com o cliente: explica o porquê de uma mudança e tranquiliza o cliente, usando linkers de causa e consequência.
lessons.overview:
Today is the site work, not the blueprint. On Monday you studied the rule of linkers; now you use that structure in a real conversation. The executive move is simple and powerful: before dropping the news, you give the background and only then present the fact. Clients like Microsoft, Amazon and Google do not fear problems — they fear being caught by surprise.

The scenario of this lesson is to give a heads-up about a small supply delay. You will practice the three-step sequence: signal the context ("Let me walk you through the reason"), point out what happened and then reassure the client by showing that everything is under control. The key word of the module is transparency: you open up the why, but always with a plan in hand.

For Fábio, this is the most common scene in the monthly relationship meetings. A good operations director knows how to turn bad news into proof of good management: he had a contingency ready, he acted to mitigate the risk and he keeps the client informed — "I'll keep you posted". This is where long-term trust between companies is born.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora para a simulação de hoje: "Before I share the update, let me walk you through the reason." e "It is under control, and I'll keep you posted."

Lembre da ordem: contexto, causa, consequência — e feche tranquilizando o cliente.
lessons.situation: Reunião mensal com o gerente de conta da Google. Houve um pequeno atraso no fornecimento de equipamentos e você precisa comunicar isso sem abalar a confiança.
lessons.context: Before I share the update, let me walk you through the reason. One supplier had a customs delay, so two generators arrived late. Because we had a backup supplier ready, the schedule does not change. It is fully under control, and I'll keep you posted.

vocab.example: Let me give you some background first.

vocab.en: to walk you through the reason
vocab.pt: explicar passo a passo o motivo
vocab.example: Let me walk you through the reason for the change.
I have a quick update on the site.

The situation is under control.
I want to reassure you about the date.
In short, the deadline stays the same.
We work with full transparency.

exercises.explanation: Repita até soar natural. O segredo é o tom: tranquilo e no controle.

exercises.title: 6. Tranquilize o cliente

exercises.translation: Tínhamos um fornecedor reserva pronto, então o cronograma não muda. Está sob controle.
exercises.prompt: Leia em voz alta fechando a explicação. Termine transmitindo segurança.
exercises.explanation: Causa, consequência e tranquilização numa frase só. É o fechamento que mantém a confiança.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em 15-20 segundos, faça um role-play sozinho: dê um heads-up à Google sobre um pequeno atraso. Comece pelo contexto, explique a causa, e feche dizendo que está under control. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can open with the context before I share an update.
I can explain the cause and then the consequence.
I can reassure a client and say it is under control.
I can promise to keep the client posted.

lessons.title: Reported speech para escuta ativa e confirmação de entendimento
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você confirma o que o cliente disse e checa o seu entendimento, usando reported speech simples como 'You said that...', 'You mentioned that...' e 'You asked if...'.
lessons.overview:
Active listening is a relationship skill, not a grammar one — but it needs a structure to work in English. When Fábio repeats, in his own words, what the client just said, he shows attention and avoids misunderstandings in high-value contracts. The tool for this is reported speech: instead of quoting the exact sentence, you report the idea.

The rule is straightforward and fits the A2+ level. You use a reporting verb in the past plus 'that' (which can be omitted): you said that, you mentioned that, you asked if. In questions, the order changes to an affirmative sentence: the question "Is the budget fixed?" becomes "You asked if the budget was fixed." The verb usually steps back one tense (say → said; is → was), but in everyday executive life what matters is clarity, not perfection.

These verbs support three golden moves in monthly meetings: to confirm, to recap and to make sure we are aligned. Closing a meeting block with "Let me recap the main points to make sure we are aligned" gives the Microsoft, Amazon or Google client the certainty that they were heard. This is the blueprint; on Friday you lead the relationship meeting using this listening.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora que voltarão na prática: "You said that the deadline was important." e "Let me recap to make sure we are aligned."

Regra rápida: verbo de relato no passado + (that) + ideia. Em perguntas, use 'if/whether' e ordem de frase afirmativa.
lessons.situation: Numa call com a Amazon, o cliente expôs três pedidos. Antes de responder, você confirma cada ponto para mostrar que ouviu com atenção.
lessons.context: Let me recap to make sure we are aligned. You said that the deadline was the top priority. You mentioned that the budget was fixed. And you asked if we could add a night shift. Did I get that right?

lessons.title: Reunião mensal de relacionamento — rodízio Microsoft/Amazon/Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você conduz uma reunião mensal de relacionamento com o cliente, confirmando status e definindo próximos passos com escuta ativa e contextualização.
lessons.overview:
Today is the site work: you simulate the monthly relationship meeting that rotates among Microsoft, Amazon and Google. There is no new grammar — you bring together what you already have: giving context before presenting (lessons 25-26) and confirming what the client says (lesson 27). The goal is to keep the relationship strong, meeting after meeting.

The meeting script has a clear shape. You open to reconnect and touch base: "Thanks for the time. Let's touch base on the project." Then comes the status update, with a highlight of the month: what moved forward on your side and on the client's side — on your side / on ours. You use a dashboard to outline the numbers in a visual and direct way.

The closing is what builds long-term trust: you define the next steps and each action item with a deadline — often by month-end. And you promise to circle back at the next meeting. The message Fábio wants to leave with each big data client is simple and strong: "You are in good hands."

lessons.title: Condicionais (0, 1, 2): a estrutura do "if" na negociação
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa os condicionais 0, 1 e 2 para negociar com clareza, ligando uma condição a um resultado com 'if + present' e 'if + past, would'.
lessons.overview:
Negotiating is, at its core, talking about conditions: "if this, then that". For an operations director discussing price, deadline and scope with Microsoft, Amazon and Google, mastering 'if' is the central structure of Pillar 2. Whoever knows how to build a conditional sentence can defend margin, propose trades and lock in a deal without sounding aggressive.

There are three conditionals, and the logic is precise. The zero conditional (if + present, present) is for truths and rules: "If the scope grows, the cost grows." The first conditional (if + present, will) is for real and likely situations at the table: "If you confirm the volume, we will hold the price." The second conditional (if + past, would) is for hypotheses, softer offers and scenarios: "If you signed for two years, we would offer a better unit price." The golden rule: in the second conditional, the past ('signed') does not talk about the past — it talks about a hypothesis.

These three molds carry the vocabulary of negotiation: to hold a price, unit price, scope, trade-off and the connectors provided that and as long as. The outcome of each condition becomes clear, and that protects the safety of execution. This is the blueprint; on Friday you negotiate engineering cost with AWS using these sentences.
lessons.intro:
Âncoras que voltam na prática: "If you confirm the volume, we will hold the price." e "If you signed for two years, we would offer a better price."

Regra: 1º condicional = situação real (if + present, will). 2º condicional = hipótese (if + past, would).
lessons.situation: Você prepara a estrutura das frases que dirá à AWS: como ligar uma condição (volume, prazo, escopo) a um resultado (preço, prazo de entrega).
lessons.context: If the scope grows, the cost grows. That is a simple rule. If you confirm the volume this week, we will hold the current price. And if you signed a two-year contract, we would offer a better unit price. The outcome depends on the condition.

options.whyWrong: Misturou os condicionais. Para hipótese (segundo condicional), use 'if + past' (signed) com 'would'.

options.text: If you signed for two years, we would give a better price.

options.whyWrong: No segundo condicional o par é 'signed ... would', não 'signed ... will'.

exercises.explanation: Segundo condicional = hipótese: if + past (signed) + would. O passado aqui não fala do passado, fala de um cenário.

commonErrors.would hold: Para uma condição real e provável, use 'will hold', não 'would hold'.

exercises.title: 3. Monte a regra (condicional zero)
exercises.explanation: Condicional zero para uma verdade da engenharia: if + present, present. Mais escopo, mais custo — é regra, não hipótese.

would offer|would give|if you signed|unit price

exercises.explanation: Primeiro condicional para o que é real agora; segundo condicional para uma oferta hipotética. Os dois protegem a sua margem.

lessons.title: Negociando custo de N atividades de engenharia com a AWS
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você negocia o custo de atividades de engenharia com a AWS, defendendo o preço e propondo trocas com frases de negociação no nível executivo.
lessons.overview:
Today is the site work: you sit at the table with AWS to negotiate the cost of an engineering package with several activities. There is no new grammar — you apply Monday's conditionals in a real simulation. The goal is to defend the price calmly, show value and reach a fair agreement, without losing the long-term relationship.

The negotiation has typical moves that you will train. The client will push back and ask you to come down on price. Your defense is to break down the cost and walk through the numbers, showing the labor cost and the value for money. When you have to give ground, give it with a trade: "I can come down a little in exchange for a longer contract." — that is the in exchange for.

Some positions are non-negotiable, like the safety of execution, and that needs to be made clear with polite firmness. Others allow you to meet halfway. And beware of scope creep: every new activity goes into the price. Fábio closes by seeking a firm price that he can justify internally. This is the real, everyday negotiation with the big data clients.
lessons.intro:
Âncoras para o role-play: "Let me walk you through the numbers." e "I can come down a little in exchange for a longer contract."

Lembre: detalhe o custo, ceda só com troca, e marque o que é non-negotiable (a segurança).

lessons.title: Comparativos e superlativos: ancorando valor e preço
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue comparar a Racional com o mercado usando comparativos (mais... que) e superlativos (o mais...), para ancorar valor e preço antes de negociar.
lessons.overview:
Every negotiation starts long before the price. It starts when you position your company side by side with the others. In English, this is done with comparatives and superlatives. When a big data client like Google evaluates a builder for a data center, they don't only ask "how much does it cost?". They ask "why you, and not the competitor?". The answer is a comparison: we are faster than the market, we have the strongest safety record.

For Racional's Operations Director, this is the language of someone who arrives with five decades of projects. You don't need to attack anyone: you simply show the numbers and facts the company already has. More than 620 projects delivered, more than 10 million square meters, more than 50 years in the market. Each of these data points becomes a natural comparison: the most experienced partner in the region, with better value across the entire project.

Today's goal is not to speak yet — it is to understand the rule before applying it. As an engineer, you want the blueprint before the build. So let's look at the exact structure: when to use -er, when to use more, when to use the -est or the most, and the irregulars that show up all the time (good, better, the best). Once Monday's rule is mastered, on Friday you use it out loud with the client.
lessons.intro:
Na sexta você vai ancorar valor diante do cliente. Hoje prepare três frases-âncora: "Our delivery is faster than the market." (comparativo curto com -er), "Our process is more reliable." (comparativo longo com more) e "We have the strongest safety record." (superlativo com the).

Repare na lógica: palavra curta ganha -er / the -est; palavra longa ganha more / the most. A comparação de dois fecha sempre com than.
lessons.situation: Na preparação para a reunião de sexta com o Google, você estuda como comparar a Racional com o mercado para justificar o valor antes de falar em preço.
lessons.context: Let me put our offer in context. Our delivery is faster than the market average. Our process is more reliable because we have fifty years of work. On safety, we have the strongest record in the segment. That is the most important point for a data center. This is better value, not a higher price.

vocab.example: One contract is cheaper than three.
Our schedule is faster than the market.
Our team is more reliable than the average.
This price is more competitive this year.
We run the safest sites in the region.
We have the strongest safety record.
We are the most experienced team here.
It is better value for the full project.
This is the best option for the timeline.
Our method is faster than theirs.
We outperform the market on delivery.
Our track record is very strong.
We beat the market benchmark.
A good comparison anchors the value.

exercises.title: 1. Palavra curta ou longa?
exercises.prompt: Como se forma o comparativo de 'reliable' (palavra longa)?

options.whyWrong: '-er' só vale para palavras curtas (1 sílaba). 'Reliable' é longa, então usa 'more'.
Nunca os dois juntos. Ou 'more reliable' (longa) ou '-er' (curta), jamais os dois.

exercises.explanation: Palavra longa = 'more' + adjetivo. Palavra curta = adjetivo + '-er'. Nunca os dois ao mesmo tempo.

exercises.title: 2. Comparativo curto com 'than'
exercises.prompt: Our delivery is ___ (fast) than the market average.
exercises.explanation: 'Fast' é curta (1 sílaba): comparativo = fast + -er = 'faster'. A comparação fecha com 'than'.

commonErrors.more fast: Palavra curta não usa 'more'. O certo é 'faster'.
commonErrors.fastest: 'Fastest' é superlativo (contra todos). Aqui você compara com um, então 'faster than'.

exercises.title: 3. Monte o superlativo de segurança
exercises.explanation: Superlativo curto = 'the' + adjetivo + '-est': 'the strongest'. O 'the' é obrigatório no superlativo.

exercises.title: 4. Combine a forma com a regra
exercises.explanation: Curta usa -er/-est; longa usa more/most; e há os irregulares (good/bad). Quatro padrões cobrem quase tudo.

exercises.title: 5. Ancore o valor da Racional (2 frases)
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases posicionando a Racional para o Google: uma com comparativo + 'than', outra com superlativo + 'the'. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
keywords: faster than|cheaper than|more reliable|more competitive|better value|than
the safest|the strongest|the most experienced|the best|track record
exercises.modelAnswer: Our delivery is faster than the market average, and our process is more reliable. On safety, we have the strongest track record in the segment.
exercises.explanation: Comparativo (contra o mercado) + superlativo (contra todos) = um ancoramento que justifica o preço antes de falar dele.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em cerca de 15 segundos, posicione a Racional contra o mercado usando um comparativo (com 'than') e um superlativo (com 'the'). Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can form comparatives with '-er' for short words and 'more' for long words.
I can form superlatives with 'the -est' or 'the most'.
I can use the irregulars good, better, the best.
I can compare with 'than' and anchor value before I name a price.
I can position Racional as the strongest option with a superlative.

lessons.title: Defendendo margem e valores expressivos sem perder a relação
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue defender a margem e valores expressivos diante da Microsoft, usando comparações para justificar o preço sem perder a relação.
lessons.overview:
When the client says "the price is high", the instinct is to lower it. The experienced executive does the opposite: he defends a margin. Defending a margin is not stubbornness — it is showing, through comparison, why that price delivers more. For Racional, which competes for contracts worth hundreds of millions with Microsoft, Amazon and Google, knowing how to sustain a significant value without sounding defensive is one of the most valuable commercial skills in the market.

The logic is simple and has three steps. First, you acknowledge the client's perception: to put it in context. Then, you anchor with the comparison you studied on Monday: we are faster, more reliable, with the best track record. Finally, you translate this into a real benefit: fewer delays, less risk, return on investment. A data center that runs late costs far more than any discount you could give.

This is a PRACTICE lesson: no new rule. Today you speak. We will simulate the meeting in which the Microsoft account manager questions your margin, and you answer as a long-term partner — firm on price, open on the relationship. The weight is on oral production with the teacher: dictate, build the sentence and say it out loud until it comes out naturally.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você usa, em voz alta, a comparação de segunda para defender valor. Frases-âncora: "Let me put it in context.", "That means fewer delays and less risk." e "This is better value, not a higher price."

Tom de parceiro: calmo, firme, sem pedir desculpa pelo preço.
lessons.situation: Reunião com o gerente de conta da Microsoft. Ele acha o valor da proposta alto e questiona a margem. Você defende o preço comparando e traduzindo em benefício, mantendo a relação.
lessons.context: I hear you. The figure is significant, and I respect that. But let me put it in context. Our delivery is faster than the market, and our safety record is the strongest in the segment. That means fewer delays and less risk. So this is better value, not a higher price. We want to be your long-term partner.

vocab.example: I can defend a margin with facts.
It is a significant figure, I agree.
Let me put it in context for you.
Our record helps us justify the price.
You pay a small premium for safety.
Quality translates into fewer delays.
The return on investment is clear.
Over the project, the numbers add up.
Good planning means fewer delays.
A strong team means less risk.
I hold firm, but I stay polite.
This is better value for you.
We want to be a long-term partner.
I reframe price as value.

exercises.title: 1. Ditado: reconhecer e contextualizar
exercises.correctText: The figure is significant, but let me put it in context.
exercises.explanation: Reconhecer a percepção ('significant') e abrir o argumento ('put it in context') é o primeiro passo para defender a margem.

exercises.title: 2. Ditado: traduzir em benefício
exercises.correctText: That means fewer delays and less risk for you.
exercises.explanation: Note 'fewer delays' (contável) e 'less risk' (não contável). Traduzir força em benefício é o que sustenta o preço.

exercises.title: 3. Monte a frase de reposicionamento
exercises.explanation: Reposicione preço como valor: 'This is better value, not a higher price.' É a frase que fecha a defesa de margem.

exercises.title: 4. Defenda a margem em voz alta
exercises.targetText: I hear you. But our delivery is faster and our record is the strongest. That means fewer delays and less risk. This is better value, not a higher price.
exercises.translation: Eu entendo. Mas nossa entrega é mais rápida e nosso histórico é o melhor. Isso significa menos atrasos e menos risco. Isso é melhor custo-benefício, não um preço mais alto.
exercises.prompt: Leia em voz alta como se respondesse ao gerente da Microsoft que achou o valor alto. Tom calmo e firme.
exercises.explanation: Reconhecer, ancorar, traduzir, reposicionar. Repita até fechar em 'better value, not a higher price' sem hesitar.

lessons.critical: Imagine que a Microsoft acabou de dizer que sua margem está alta. Em voz alta, em cerca de 20 segundos, defenda o valor comparando e traduzindo em benefício, sem dar desconto. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can acknowledge a price concern without apologizing.
I can put the price in context with a comparison.
I can translate a strength into fewer delays and less risk.
I can reframe a high price as better value.
I can hold firm on margin and keep the relationship.

lessons.title: Future forms, deadlines e schedule language
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue falar de prazos e cronograma usando as formas de futuro do inglês (will, going to, present continuous) para comprometer datas com clareza.
lessons.overview:
On a project, a deadline is a commitment. And talking about deadlines in English requires knowing how to choose the right future form. English has three main paths: will + verb (decision/promise in the moment), going to + verb (a plan already decided) and the present continuous with future meaning (a confirmed schedule). For the timeline of an Amazon data center, each one says something different — and the client notices the difference.

Schedule vocabulary is as important as the grammar. You will say that something is on schedule or that it might fall behind. You will mark a milestone, agree on the kickoff date and the hand over of each phase. You will use prepositions that confuse many Brazilians: by (up to a deadline) and within (inside a period). "By Friday" and "within two weeks" are not the same thing, and getting this wrong changes the contract.

As an engineer, you recognize here the logic of the critical path: the rule before the build. Today is THEORY — you study and fix the structure. On Friday, you use all of this to negotiate, out loud, a real schedule with the client. Master the three future forms and the date vocabulary, and you start committing to deadlines with the precision Racional already has in the field.
lessons.intro:
Na sexta você vai negociar datas. Hoje prepare a estrutura: "We will hand over phase one by March." (will + by = data limite), "We are going to add a shift." (plano decidido) e "The kickoff is starting on Monday." (agenda confirmada).

Lembre: by = até uma data; within = dentro de um período.
lessons.situation: Na preparação para a sexta com a Amazon, você estuda as formas de futuro e o vocabulário de cronograma para comprometer prazos com clareza.
lessons.context: Here is the plan for the data center. We will start on Monday. We are going to deliver phase one by March. The cooling system is due within four weeks. We are on schedule, and we will not fall behind. Each milestone is clear, and we will hand over each phase on time.

vocab.example: We will start on Monday.
We are going to add a team.
We are meeting the client on Friday.
We will finish by March.
It is ready within two weeks.
The report is due on Friday.
The first milestone is the foundation.
We hand over phase one in March.
The lead time for steel is six weeks.
The project is on schedule.
We will not fall behind.
Phase two starts in April.
We commission the system in May.
The kickoff date is March first.

exercises.title: 1. Qual forma de futuro?
exercises.prompt: O cliente pergunta a data de início. A agenda já está marcada para segunda. Qual frase é a mais natural?

options.text: We will maybe start one day.
options.whyWrong: 'Will maybe' soa vago e sem compromisso. Para uma agenda já marcada, use o presente contínuo.
Falta a referência de tempo e a ideia de agenda confirmada. Use o presente contínuo com a data: 'starting on Monday'.

exercises.explanation: Agenda já marcada = present continuous com valor de futuro: 'We are starting on Monday.'

exercises.title: 2. 'By' ou 'within'?
exercises.prompt: We will hand over phase one ___ March.
exercises.explanation: 'By' aponta para uma data limite (até março). 'Within' seria para um período ('within four weeks').

commonErrors.within: 'Within' é para um período (within four weeks). Para uma data limite, use 'by'.
commonErrors.until: 'Until' é para ação contínua até um ponto. Para um prazo de entrega, use 'by'.

exercises.title: 3. Monte a promessa de entrega
exercises.explanation: Plano já decidido = 'going to' + verbo. A data limite fecha com 'by March'.

exercises.title: 4. Combine o termo com o sentido
exercises.explanation: Vocabulário de cronograma: marco, entrega, no prazo, atrasar. São as palavras que você usa na sexta.

exercises.title: 5. Escreva o plano de prazo (2 frases)
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases sobre o cronograma de um data center: uma com uma forma de futuro (will / going to / present continuous) e uma com 'by' ou 'within'. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta aula. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: We will hand over phase one by March, and we are on schedule. The cooling system is due within four weeks.
exercises.explanation: Forma de futuro + preposição de prazo = um compromisso de cronograma claro e profissional.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em cerca de 15 segundos, descreva o plano de prazo de uma obra usando uma forma de futuro e 'by' ou 'within'. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can use 'will' for a promise and 'going to' for a plan.
I can use the present continuous for a fixed schedule.
I can use 'by' for a deadline and 'within' for a period.
I can talk about milestones, phases, and handover dates.
I can say if a project is on schedule or may fall behind.

lessons.title: Negociando prazos correlacionados a custo (cronograma do data center)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue negociar, em voz alta, prazos ligados a custo com a Amazon, explicando o trade-off entre comprimir o cronograma e o custo extra.
lessons.overview:
In the world of data centers, time is money in a literal way. The client wants the project sooner; compressing the timeline almost always has a price. Knowing how to lead this conversation — the trade-off between cost and time — is the heart of deadline negotiation. You don't just say "yes" or "no": you show what changes in each scenario.

There are concrete levers Racional can pull. You can add shifts, fast-track certain phases or bring forward a delivery — but each one has an extra cost. Or you can push back the deadline and protect the schedule buffer. The secret is letting the client choose with information: "what matters more to you, time or cost?".

This is a PRACTICE lesson, so no new rule. You will simulate the conversation with the Amazon project manager who asks for the data center sooner. Your role is to be realistic and honest: commit only to what the project can deliver, show what it costs to bring things forward, and, when possible, offer something at no extra cost. Today's weight is on speaking: dictation, sentence building and role-play out loud with the teacher.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você negocia prazo em voz alta. Frases-âncora: "We can fast-track it, but it adds an extra cost.", "There is a trade-off between cost and time." e "What matters more to you, the date or the cost?"

Seja realista: prometa só o que a obra entrega.
lessons.situation: Reunião com o gerente de projeto da Amazon. Ele quer o data center pronto antes do prazo. Você explica o trade-off entre comprimir o cronograma e o custo extra, e ajuda o cliente a escolher.
lessons.context: I understand you want the data center earlier. We can fast-track it, but there is a trade-off between cost and time. To bring it forward, we add shifts, and that means an extra cost. If you prefer no extra cost, we push back the deadline a little. What matters more to you, the date or the cost? Let us lock a realistic date together.

vocab.example: We can compress the schedule a little.
We can fast-track the first phase.
There is a trade-off between cost and time.
We add shifts to go faster.
We can bring the date forward.
We push back the deadline by one week.

Time and cost correlate closely.
The cooling system is on the critical path.
We keep a small buffer for safety.
Let us lock the date today.
I prefer a realistic date.
We can do that at no extra cost.
What matters more, time or cost?

exercises.explanation: A frase central da negociação de prazo: mostrar que correr e custo andam juntos.

exercises.title: 2. Ditado: acelerar tem custo
exercises.correctText: We can fast-track it, but it adds an extra cost.
exercises.explanation: Você aceita acelerar ('fast-track'), mas deixa claro o custo extra. Honesto e realista.

exercises.title: 3. Monte a pergunta de escolha

lessons.critical: Imagine que a Amazon pediu o data center um mês antes. Em voz alta, em cerca de 20 segundos, explique o trade-off entre prazo e custo e ajude o cliente a escolher. Sem texto na frente.

lessons.title: Vocabulário contratual: scope, change order, claim
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue usar o vocabulário contratual essencial — scope, change order e claim — entendendo o que cada termo significa e quando usá-lo.
lessons.overview:
A construction contract is a map of what was agreed. Knowing how to talk about it in English protects Racional and protects the relationship with the client. Three words form the backbone: scope of work (what was contracted), change order (when something new comes in) and claim (when you have a right to extra cost or time). Confusing these three is expensive.

The logic is clear. If a client request is out of scope, you neither refuse it nor do it for free: you raise a change order, which brings additional cost and, sometimes, a time extension. If the delay came from the client's side and you have a right guaranteed by a clause, you file a claim. And none of this counts verbally: everything must be in writing and approved.

For the Operations Director who negotiates with Microsoft, Amazon and Google, this is the language that separates the professional from the amateur. As an engineer, you like the rule before the build: today is THEORY, you fix each term and the sentence structure. On Friday, you use all of this to lead, out loud, a change order conversation with Google.
lessons.intro:
Na sexta você vai conduzir uma conversa de alteração contratual. Hoje fixe as três frases-âncora: "This is out of scope.", "It requires a change order." e "It must be approved in writing."

Lembre da diferença: change order = trabalho novo; claim = direito a custo/prazo extra.
lessons.situation: Na preparação para a sexta com o Google, você estuda o vocabulário contratual para saber identificar o que está fora do escopo e como formalizar uma alteração.
lessons.context: Let me be clear about the contract. The original scope covers the data hall and the cooling system. The new fire line is out of scope, so it requires a change order. A change order has an additional cost, and the client must approve it in writing. If the delay comes from your side, we may also file a claim.

vocab.example: The scope of work is in the contract.
This new line is out of scope.

lessons.title: Discutindo questões contratuais e change orders com o Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue conduzir, em voz alta, uma conversa de change order com o Google — identificar o que está fora do escopo, formalizar a alteração e mostrar o impacto.
lessons.overview:
In a project meeting, the client almost always asks for something new. The professional who knows how to lead this moment without a rushed "yes" or a blunt "no" protects the project and the relationship. The most valuable phrase here is simple: let me check. You buy time, consult the contract and answer with confidence, as per the contract.

The path is clear and polite. You acknowledge the request, check whether it falls outside the scope, and then propose to issue a change order. You flag the cost impact and the schedule impact, and you close by agreeing on the next step: putting everything in writing. When you can, you show goodwill — happy to or even absorb the cost of something small, to preserve the partnership.

This is a PRACTICE lesson, with no new rule: today you speak. We will simulate the monthly meeting with the Google project manager, who asks for a change to the data center. Your role is to lead the conversation calmly and firmly, taking the client from the informal request to the formalized change order. The weight is on oral production: dictation, sentence building and role-play out loud with the teacher.
lessons.intro:
Hoje você conduz a conversa de alteração com o cliente, em voz alta. Frases-âncora: "Let me check the contract.", "That falls outside the scope, so we issue a change order." e "I will put it in writing and get back to you."

Tom calmo, parceiro, sem prometer o que ainda não verificou.
lessons.situation: Reunião mensal com o gerente de projeto do Google. Ele pede uma alteração no data center que não estava no escopo original, e você conduz a conversa até uma change order formal.
lessons.context: I understand you want to add a second cooling loop. Let me check the contract first. The original scope covers one system, so this falls outside the scope. We are happy to do it, but we issue a change order. There is a cost impact and a schedule impact. I will flag both and put it in writing. Let me get back to you with the next step.

lessons.title: Linguagem de proposta e contraproposta (concordar/discordar/propor)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você sabe concordar, discordar com respeito e fazer uma contraproposta em inglês, usando a estrutura condicional 'If you..., we can...'.
lessons.overview:
Negotiating with a client like Microsoft or AWS is not only about price. Before any number, you need to know how to react to what the other side says: agree when it makes sense, disagree without closing the door and offer an alternative. At Racional, with more than 50 years of delivered projects, the operations director does this all the time: he hears the data center client's demand, shows what is possible and proposes a path. In English, these three functions have ready-made phrases — to agree, to push back and counterproposal.

The most important point is how you disagree. In business English, starting with a blunt "No" sounds aggressive and can cool the relationship. The professional path is to use a cushion: I see your point or I'm afraid before saying that something doesn't work. This way you protect the long-term relationship, which is the heart of our program, without giving up your commercial position.

The heart of the lesson is the counterproposal. Every time you give something on a project — a deadline, a price, a scope — you ask for something in return. The tool for this is the conditional: "If you extend the deadline, we can hold the price." Whoever masters this two-half bridge (condition + offer) leads the negotiation with Microsoft, Amazon or Google instead of just reacting to it.
lessons.intro:
A regra da contraproposta tem duas metades: uma condição ("If you...") e uma oferta ("we can..."). Você troca uma coisa por outra na mesma frase. Exemplos: "If you accept a phased delivery, we can hold the original price." / "If you extend the deadline, we can reduce the cost."

Para concordar: "That works for us". Para discordar com respeito: "I see your point, but I'm afraid that doesn't work for us." Note a ordem: amortecedor primeiro, discordância depois, contraproposta no fim.
lessons.situation: Antes da reunião de sexta com a AWS, você estuda as frases para concordar com um ponto, discordar de outro com respeito e oferecer uma contraproposta.
lessons.context: I see your point about the timeline, and I agree the date is important to you. However, I'm afraid the price you suggested doesn't work for us at this scope. Here is what I can offer: if you accept delivery in two phases, we can hold the original price. In return, we keep the same quality on site. Would that work on your side?

vocab.en: to be on the same page

lessons.title: Barganha: trade-offs prazo × custo × escopo sob pressão
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue barganhar em voz alta sob pressão, defendendo o trade-off entre prazo, custo e escopo com um cliente big tech.
lessons.overview:
Every project lives off three variables that pull on each other: time, cost and scope. This is the negotiation triangle. The client — AWS building a new data center, for example — almost always wants to improve all three at once: faster, cheaper and with more deliverables. The role of Racional's operations director is to show, calmly, that touching one variable puts pressure on the others. Whoever names the trade-off leads the conversation.

Today is the practice: you will bargain live with the teacher, under pressure. The anchor is the conditional counterproposal you studied on Monday, now applied to the triangle: "If you want it faster, the cost goes up", "If you want a lower price, we cut the scope", "If you can extend the deadline, we can hold the cost." There is no new theory; the focus is speaking firmly and not filling the silence with a free concession.

The secret under pressure is simple: breathe, repeat the trade-off and hand the choice back to the client — "Which matters most to you, the date or the price?" This moves you out of the position of someone who only gives ground and into the position of someone who leads. For Racional, which protects its margin and its track record of 620+ projects, defending the triangle is defending the quality of delivery for Microsoft, Amazon and Google.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora para a simulação de hoje: "To be honest, I can't move both at once." / "If you need it faster, the cost goes up." / "Which one matters most to you, the date or the price?"

Regra: para dar uma variável, peça outra. Nunca ceda nas três.
lessons.situation: Reunião de negociação com a AWS, sob pressão. O gerente de conta quer entrega mais rápida E preço menor ao mesmo tempo, e você precisa defender o trade-off sem ceder tudo.
lessons.context: I hear you. You would like it faster and at a lower price. I have to be honest: I can't move both at once. Here is the trade-off. If you need the earlier date, the cost goes up, because we add a second crew. If the budget is fixed, we keep the original timeline. So, which one matters most to you right now, the date or the price?

vocab.example: There is always a trade-off in a contract.

lessons.title: Terceira condicional & mixed: revisitando decisões passadas
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa a terceira condicional e a condicional mista para falar de decisões passadas e seus efeitos, sem soar acusador.
lessons.overview:
In a negotiation, you often need to look back. When a client approval was delayed and the project schedule suffered, Racional's operations director needs to explain the effect of this without picking a fight. In English, the tool for this is the third conditional: talking about what would have happened if the past had been different. It is a structure that gives weight and clarity to your argument in a meeting with Google or AWS.

This lesson is precise: the rule comes before the application. The third conditional has a fixed skeleton — If + had + participle, ... would have + participle. Example: "If you had approved it earlier, we would have finished on time." There is also the mixed conditional, when the cause is in the past and the effect is now: "If we had signed last month, we would be on site today." Memorizing this skeleton is what unlocks the verb tense in the moment of speaking.

The business value is great: the third conditional shows consequence without pointing fingers. Instead of saying "it was your fault", you say "if X had happened, Y would have happened" — it sounds analytical and professional. For Racional, which builds long-term relationships with big data clients, talking about the past with elegance protects trust and prepares the next change order.
lessons.intro:
Esqueleto da terceira condicional: If + had + particípio na condição, would have + particípio no resultado. Ex.: "If you had approved it earlier, we would have finished on time."

Condicional mista (causa passada, efeito agora): If + had + particípio, ... would + verbo. Ex.: "If we had signed last month, we would be on site today."
lessons.situation: Antes da reunião de sexta com o Google, você estuda como explicar, sem acusar, que um atraso de aprovação do cliente causou impacto no cronograma.
lessons.context: Let me put this in perspective. If we had received the approval in March, we would have started the cooling installation on time. And if that delay had not happened, we would be in the testing phase right now. I am not pointing fingers. I just want us to learn from it for the next change order.

vocab.example: Let me put this in perspective.

I am not pointing fingers.
Let's learn from it for next time.

That is a clear lesson learned.

exercises.title: 1. Mostrar consequência sem acusar
exercises.prompt: Você quer explicar o impacto de um atraso de aprovação ao Google, sem soar acusador. Qual frase é a melhor?

options.text: You were late, so it's your fault.
options.whyWrong: Aponta o dedo e quebra a confiança. A terceira condicional mostra a consequência sem acusar.

options.text: If you had approved it earlier, we would have finished on time.
If you approve it earlier, we finish on time.
options.whyWrong: Essa é a primeira condicional (presente/futuro). Para falar de um passado que não aconteceu, use 'had approved' + 'would have finished'.

exercises.title: 2. O resultado da terceira condicional
exercises.prompt: If we had received the approval in March, we ___ have started the work on time.

lessons.title: Tréplica: defendendo posição na 2ª e 3ª troca da reunião
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você defende sua posição com respeito na segunda e terceira troca de uma reunião, mantendo a relação aberta.
lessons.overview:
The first answer in a negotiation is easy. The hard part is the rebuttal: when the client comes back with pressure a second and a third time. That is where most people give ground without realizing it. Racional's operations director, in a meeting with Microsoft or AWS, needs to stand firm without sounding stubborn and without closing the door on the relationship.

Today is the practice: you will train the second and third exchange out loud with the teacher. There is no new grammar. The anchors are rebuttal phrases: "My position hasn't changed, and here is why", "That's a fair point, but not on price", "I hear you, and I'm happy to move on scope, but not on safety." The secret is separating what is negotiable from what is non-negotiable.

Defending a position is also caring for the long-term relationship, one of the pillars of our program. That is why the rebuttal always acknowledges the other side before holding the point: "I hear you", "with respect", "that's a fair point." You keep firm and look for common ground, closing with a question that keeps the conversation alive: "Where does that leave us?" For Racional, with 620+ projects of credibility, holding a position with elegance is what protects the margin and the trust of the big data client.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora para a simulação: "My position hasn't changed, and here's why." / "That's a fair point, but not on price." / "With respect, safety is non-negotiable."

Feche sempre devolvendo a palavra: "Where does that leave us?"
lessons.situation: Segunda e terceira troca de uma reunião com a Microsoft. O cliente insiste no mesmo desconto, e você precisa segurar a posição sem fechar a porta.
lessons.context: I hear you, and that is a fair point. But my position hasn't changed, and here is why: at this price, we can't keep the same safety standard on site. With respect, safety is non-negotiable for us. I am happy to move on the timeline, but not on that. So, where does that leave us? Let's find some common ground.

We need to stand firm on safety.

lessons.title: Linguagem de segurança de execução: risk, assurance & guarantees
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa a linguagem de risco, garantia e compromisso para dar segurança ao cliente sobre a execução da obra.
lessons.overview:
For a client like Amazon or Google, the biggest fear in a construction contract is not the price — it is the risk that execution will fail: delays, defects, safety problems. Racional's edge, with more than 50 years and 10 million square meters built, is precisely the ability to provide assurance that the data center will be delivered exactly as promised. This lesson teaches the language of that confidence.

As an exact-sciences lesson, the rule comes first. You will learn the difference between talking about risk and giving a guarantee. For risk, verbs like to mitigate and to flag a risk show that you see the problem before it happens. For the guarantee, phrases like to ensure, to safeguard and to honor a commitment show that you take responsibility for it. A contingency plan is the concrete proof that you have thought about the worst-case scenario.

The commercial effect of this language is to give the client peace of mind. When you say that Racional is reliable and show its track record, you turn a promise into perceived security. On Friday, you will use all of this in a role-play; today, you draw the blueprint of these phrases before you step onto the construction site of the conversation with the big-data client.
lessons.intro:
Duas famílias de frases. Risco: "We flag the risk early and we have a plan to mitigate it." Garantia: "We ensure the quality, we safeguard the timeline, and we honor our commitments."

Frase-modelo forte: "We have a contingency plan for the worst-case scenario, so you have peace of mind."
lessons.situation: Antes da reunião de sexta com a Amazon, você estuda como mostrar que a Racional vê os riscos e garante a entrega da obra.
lessons.context: Let me be clear about how we manage risk. We flag any risk early, and we have a plan to mitigate it. We ensure the quality of the work, and we safeguard the timeline with a contingency plan for the worst-case scenario. Our track record speaks for itself: we are reliable, and we always honor our commitments. That should give you peace of mind.

vocab.example: Every project has some risk.
We have a plan to mitigate the risk.
I can give you that assurance.
We ensure the quality of the work.
We offer a guarantee on the work.
We safeguard the timeline.
We have a contingency plan ready.
We flag a risk early.
Our team is reliable.
Our track record speaks for itself.
We always honor our commitments.
We plan for the worst-case scenario.
That gives the client peace of mind.

options.whyWrong: 'Maybe' soa incerto. Para dar segurança, mostre o plano: flag, mitigate, contingency plan.

options.text: We flag risks early and we have a contingency plan to safeguard the timeline.

options.whyWrong: Vago e fraco. Garantia real vem de um plano concreto, não de 'don't worry'.

exercises.explanation: 'To ensure' = assegurar que algo aconteça. É o verbo central da linguagem de garantia.

commonErrors.assure: 'Assure' é tranquilizar uma pessoa; para um resultado/coisa, use 'ensure'.

exercises.title: 3. Monte a frase do plano de contingência
exercises.explanation: Um plano de contingência para o pior cenário é a prova concreta de que você pensou no risco antes que ele aconteça.

exercises.title: 4. Combine o termo com o significado
exercises.explanation: Esses termos transformam uma promessa em segurança percebida pelo cliente.

exercises.title: 5. Sua garantia de execução (2 frases)
exercises.prompt: A Amazon teme um atraso na obra. Escreva 2 frases: (1) mostre que vocês veem o risco e (2) dê a garantia da entrega. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta lição. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
keywords: risk|to flag a risk|to mitigate|worst-case scenario
to ensure|to safeguard|contingency plan|track record|peace of mind|reliable
exercises.modelAnswer: We flag any risk early and we have a contingency plan to mitigate it. We ensure the quality and we safeguard the timeline, so you have peace of mind.
exercises.explanation: Ver o risco + dar a garantia = confiança. Você mostra que pensou no problema antes e que responde pela entrega.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em 15 a 20 segundos, tranquilize a Amazon sobre a execução da obra: mostre que a Racional vê o risco e dê a garantia da entrega, terminando com 'peace of mind'. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can talk about risk with 'to flag a risk' and 'to mitigate'.
I can give assurance with 'to ensure' and 'to safeguard'.
I can show a contingency plan for the worst-case scenario.
I can use our track record to give the client peace of mind.

lessons.title: Garantindo segurança na execução do empreendimento ao cliente
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você tranquiliza o cliente em voz alta, transformando preocupação em confiança com a linguagem de compromisso e acompanhamento.
lessons.overview:
In the final stretch of a negotiation, the big-data client almost always brings up one last concern about execution: what if it runs late? what if quality drops? The role of Racional's operations director is to address a concern head-on, without dodging it, and give confidence back. This practice is about delivering the final word that lets the client sign with peace of mind.

Today you practice out loud with the teacher, picking up the assurance language from Monday. The anchors are phrases of personal commitment and follow-up: "Your concern is fair, and rest assured we manage this closely", "You have my word", "We put it in writing", "We'll keep you informed, no surprises." There is no new theory; the weight is on speaking, on a calm and firm tone.

The secret is to combine three things: acknowledge the concern, give the guarantee and show the follow-up. When you say that Racional will follow through, stand behind the work and deliver on a promise, and that everything is put in writing, the Microsoft, Amazon or Google client feels that they are in safe hands. With 620+ projects delivered, Racional's track record speaks for itself — your job is to put that into simple, trustworthy words.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora para a simulação: "Your concern is fair, and rest assured we manage this closely." / "You have my word, and we put it in writing." / "We'll keep you informed. No surprises."

Estrutura: reconhecer + garantir + mostrar acompanhamento.
lessons.situation: Última rodada de uma reunião com o Google. O cliente traz uma preocupação final sobre a execução da obra, e você precisa tranquilizá-lo.
lessons.context: I hear you, and your concern is fair. Let me address it directly. We manage this closely, so rest assured there will be no surprises. We put the main points in writing, and you have my word that we stand behind our work. We will keep you informed at every step. Our track record speaks for itself, and we always deliver on our promises.

vocab.example: I hear you, and I understand.
Your concern is fair.
Let me address that concern.
We manage the work closely.

vocab.en: to put your mind at ease
vocab.example: Let me put your mind at ease.

Our track record speaks for itself.
You have my word on that.

We always follow through.
No surprises, I promise.
We will keep you informed.
We deliver on our promises.

exercises.explanation: 'Rest assured' tranquiliza o cliente; 'no surprises' promete previsibilidade na execução.

exercises.title: 2. Monte a frase do compromisso pessoal
exercises.explanation: Compromisso pessoal ('you have my word') + garantia da empresa ('we stand behind our work'). Juntos, eles passam confiança.

exercises.title: 3. Tranquilize o cliente em voz alta

takeaways: I can address a concern directly instead of avoiding it.
I can reassure the client with 'rest assured' and 'no surprises'.
I can give a personal commitment with 'you have my word'.
I can promise to follow through and keep the client informed.

lessons.title: Vocabulário de SST: safety, occupational health, environment
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você reconhece e usa o vocabulário de base de SST em inglês — safety, occupational health e environment — e sabe diferenciar o substantivo (a coisa) do adjetivo (a qualidade) ao descrever a cultura de segurança da Racional.
lessons.overview:
Occupational Health and Safety (OHS) is the third pillar of your program and the topic that is always on the table when you talk to Microsoft, Amazon/AWS or Google. Before you can defend Racional's indicators, you need the basic vocabulary in English: safety, occupational health and environment. These are the three words that open any OHS meeting with a big-data client, because it is on this tripod that these companies measure a construction partner.

For the operations director of a builder with 50+ years and 620+ projects, this vocabulary is not a detail: it is how you translate your daily site routine into English. In the workplace, every worker uses protective equipment, and the daily work is to identify each hazard and prevent each incident. Programs like "To Sabendo" and the DSMs (Safety Dialogues) are exactly the safety culture that sets Racional apart from its competitors.

This theory lesson is the blueprint of the language: here you learn to separate the noun from the quality. Safety is the thing; safe is the quality. Environment is the thing; environmental is the quality. Mastering this difference lets you speak with precision when, on Friday, you present to Microsoft that Racional keeps a safe site and protects the well-being of the teams on site.
lessons.intro:
Hoje a regra é simples e poderosa: separar o substantivo (a coisa) do adjetivo (a qualidade). "Safety" é a coisa; "safe" descreve a coisa. "Environment" é a coisa; "environmental" descreve a coisa.

Guarde estas frases-âncora para a prática: "Safety is our first priority.", "We keep the site safe." e "We protect the environment on every project."
lessons.situation: Você está preparando, em inglês, o vocabulário básico de SST que vai usar na reunião com a Microsoft. Antes da fala, precisa fixar os nomes e adjetivos que descrevem a cultura de segurança da Racional.
lessons.context: At Racional, safety comes first. Every worker on site uses protective equipment. We check the workplace every day. We look for any hazard and we try to prevent it. Our goal is simple: zero incidents. We also care about occupational health and the well-being of our teams. And we protect the environment on every project. This is our safety culture, and it makes our company strong.

vocab.example: Safety is our first priority.
We keep the site safe.
Occupational health is part of our plan.
We protect the environment.
We follow environmental rules.
We look for every hazard on site.
The workplace must be clean and safe.
Every worker uses a helmet.
Workers wear protective equipment.
We report every incident.
We want to prevent accidents.
We care about the well-being of our teams.
Our safety culture is strong.
Safety starts on site.

exercises.title: 1. Substantivo ou adjetivo?
exercises.prompt: Complete: "We keep the site ___."

options.whyWrong: "Safety" é o substantivo (a coisa). Depois de "keep the site" precisamos do adjetivo.
"Safely" é advérbio (de modo). Aqui descrevemos o canteiro, então usamos o adjetivo "safe".

exercises.title: 2. Complete a frase
exercises.prompt: Every worker on site uses ___ equipment.
exercises.explanation: "Protective equipment" = equipamento de proteção. É o termo de SST mais comum em obra.

exercises.title: 3. Monte a frase
exercises.explanation: "We want to prevent every hazard." = Queremos prevenir cada perigo. Estrutura: sujeito + want to + verbo.

exercises.title: 4. Associe o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: São os quatro nomes de base de SST que abrem qualquer reunião com a Microsoft.

exercises.title: 5. Escreva sobre a Racional
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 a 3 frases sobre a cultura de segurança da Racional. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula em inglês (por exemplo: safety, safe, worker, on site).
exercises.modelAnswer: Safety is our first priority. Every worker on site uses protective equipment. We want to prevent every incident.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso correto dos termos de SST em inglês.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, e em ~15 segundos, diga em inglês simples três coisas que a Racional faz pela segurança no canteiro. Comece com "At Racional, safety comes first...".
takeaways: I can say the words safety, occupational health, and environment.
I can use 'safe' and 'environmental' as adjectives.
I can talk about workers, hazards, and protective equipment.
I can describe our safety culture in simple English.

lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você apresenta, em conversa com a Microsoft, os principais indicadores de segurança da Racional, ligando o vocabulário de segunda a números reais de canteiro.
lessons.overview:
This Friday is the construction site: you move from vocabulary into speaking. The scenario is a meeting with Microsoft where you need to present Racional's safety record. For a big-data client, safety numbers are not bureaucracy — they are proof that the partner delivers the project without stopping and without putting people at risk.

You will practice how to guide the client through the data: to walk through the indicators, to highlight the strong points and show how Racional manages to keep teams safe. Terms like lost-time incident, near miss and working hours are the language that Microsoft expects to hear.

The weight of this lesson is on speaking with the teacher. You will pick up Monday's structure — OHS nouns and adjectives — and use it in ready-made phrases for the meeting, showing that Racional's track record makes the company stand out. This is the moment to turn loose words into a short, confident presentation.

Sem teoria nova hoje: vamos falar. Retome de segunda a diferença entre "safety" (a coisa) e "safe" (a qualidade) e use-a na simulação.

This is how we keep our teams safe. Our track record helps us stand out.

We count all working hours on site.
Our track record is long and clear.
I want to highlight one number.
Every worker has a medical check.
We run a training session every month.

We have a safety briefing every morning.
Our goal is to keep teams safe.

This indicator is very important.

lessons.title: Gramática de gráficos, percentuais e variação (dados e tendências)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você descreve gráficos, percentuais e variações em inglês, usando os verbos de tendência (rise, fall, remain stable) e as preposições certas (by, to, from) para falar de dados de conformidade.
lessons.overview:
When you sit down with Microsoft or Google to present safety, almost everything turns into a chart: indicators that go up, go down or hold steady. Knowing how to describe a trend in English is what separates "showing a number" from "telling a story with data". This theory lesson prepares you for next Friday's indicators meeting.

The central rule is simple and fits an exact-sciences mind: there is the verb (what the number does) and the preposition (how much and how far). The indicator can rise or fall; it can rise sharply, slightly or steadily. And the prepositions mark the size of the change: by (the amount of the change), to (the end point) and from... to....

For Racional, this is worth gold: you will be able to say that the compliance rate went up, that accidents went down and that the safety index remained stable at a high level. With a few verbs and three prepositions, you can describe any OHS chart clearly and professionally in front of a big-data client.
lessons.intro:
Hoje a regra é: verbo (o que o número faz) + preposição (quanto / até onde). Suba ou caia, sempre escolha entre "by" (a variação), "to" (o ponto final) e "from... to...".

Frases-âncora para a prática: "Incidents fell by 30%.", "The rate rose to 98%." e "It remained stable from January to June."
lessons.situation: Você está estudando, antes da reunião, como descrever em inglês os gráficos de segurança e conformidade que vai apresentar à Google.
lessons.context: Numbers tell a story. A line can rise, fall, or remain stable. Last year, our compliance rate rose sharply, from 90% to 98%. Incidents fell by 30%. After that, the rate remained stable for six months. This is a good trend. Overall, our safety numbers improved. To describe a chart, you only need two things: the verb and the preposition. Use 'by' for the change, 'to' for the end point, and 'from... to...' for the full range.

vocab.example: Our compliance rate rose last year.
Incidents fell last year.
The rate remained stable for six months.
Incidents fell by 30%.
The rate rose to 98%.
It went from 90% to 98%.
The number rose sharply.
It fell slightly last month.
The rate grew steadily.
This is a good trend.
Our compliance rate is high.
Compliance is very important for clients.
The number peaked in March.
Overall, our numbers improved.

exercises.title: 4. Associe o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: São os verbos-chave para descrever qualquer gráfico de segurança.

exercises.title: 5. Descreva o gráfico
exercises.prompt: Descreva em 2 a 3 frases um gráfico de conformidade da Racional que melhorou. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (por exemplo: rose, fell, by, to, trend, rate).

exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso correto dos verbos e preposições de variação.

lessons.overview:
Today is the construction site: you take the lead in an indicators meeting with Google. There is no new theory — you will use, by speaking, the chart grammar you studied on Monday. The goal is to look in command: present the chart, explain what it shows and answer questions with confidence.

You will practice the phrases that guide the client through the data: as you can see, to point out and to break down the numbers. When the client asks why, you answer with that's because and the main reason is. And when the numbers are strong, you simply say that the figures speak for themselves.

For Racional, mastering this kind of talk shows control: you compare your data against a market benchmark, say that the company can outperform the average and close by opening space for questions — to take questions. The weight of the lesson is on speaking with the teacher, in the Google scenario.

lessons.title: Linguagem de normas: must, have to, be required to
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você usa a linguagem de obrigação e norma em inglês — diferenciando must, have to e be required to — e sabe expressar proibição e ausência de obrigação sem trocar os sentidos.
lessons.overview:
Talking about OHS with Microsoft, Amazon/AWS or Google is, to a large extent, talking about rules and requirements. That is why this theory lesson delivers the grammar that supports the entire safety pillar: the verbs of obligation. Without them, you cannot say clearly what is mandatory on a site and what is not.

The rule is straightforward and fits an exact-sciences logic. Must and have to say that something is mandatory ("workers must wear a helmet"). To be required to is the more formal and impersonal version, used in standards and contracts ("all visitors are required to sign in"). And the care is with the negatives: mustn't is a prohibition (not allowed), while don't have to is the absence of obligation (no need to). Confusing the two completely changes the message.

For Racional, mastering this means defending the company with precision. You will be able to say that Racional complies with all standards, that certain procedures are non-negotiable and that the company enforces the rules with no exceptions. It is the language that puts you at the same level of rigor as the big techs.
lessons.intro:
Hoje a regra é: "must" e "have to" = obrigatório; "be required to" = a forma formal de norma. Cuidado com o negativo: "mustn't" = proibido; "don't have to" = não é preciso.

Frases-âncora para a prática: "Workers must wear a helmet.", "All visitors are required to sign in." e "You mustn't enter without a helmet."
lessons.situation: Você está estudando, antes da reunião com a AWS, como explicar em inglês as regras de segurança obrigatórias da Racional.
lessons.context: Safety rules are clear. Workers must wear a helmet on site. They have to follow every step. All visitors are required to sign in at the gate. Some rules are mandatory, with no exceptions. Be careful with the negative: 'you mustn't enter without a helmet' means it is not allowed. But 'you don't have to wear gloves here' means it is not necessary. At Racional, we comply with every standard, and we enforce the rules every day.

vocab.example: Workers must wear a helmet.
They have to follow the rules.
Visitors are required to sign in.
You mustn't enter without a helmet.
You don't have to wear gloves here.
Only trained workers are allowed to enter.
This training is mandatory.
We follow every safety rule.
We meet the highest standard.
This is a client requirement.
We comply with every rule.
We enforce the rules every day.
Helmets are mandatory, no exceptions.
All safety rules are in place.

exercises.title: 1. Proibição ou ausência de obrigação?
exercises.prompt: Você quer dizer que é PROIBIDO entrar sem capacete. Qual frase usar?

options.text: You don't have to enter without a helmet.
options.whyWrong: "Don't have to" significa "não precisa" — é ausência de obrigação, não proibição.

options.text: You mustn't enter without a helmet.
You are allowed to enter without a helmet.
options.whyWrong: "Are allowed to" significa "tem permissão" — é o oposto de proibição.

exercises.title: 2. Complete a frase formal
exercises.prompt: All visitors are ___ to sign in at the gate.
exercises.explanation: "Are required to" é a forma formal de obrigação, usada em normas e contratos.

exercises.title: 3. Monte a frase
exercises.explanation: "Workers must wear a helmet on site." Depois de "must" vem o verbo sem "to".

exercises.title: 4. Associe o termo à tradução
exercises.explanation: São os termos que você usa para defender a cultura de segurança da Racional.

exercises.title: 5. Escreva duas regras
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 a 3 frases com regras de segurança da Racional. Use ao menos 2 termos da aula (por exemplo: must, have to, required, mandatory, comply with).
exercises.modelAnswer: Workers must wear a helmet on site. All visitors are required to sign in. This rule is mandatory, with no exceptions.
exercises.explanation: A correção é só sobre o uso correto dos verbos de obrigação e dos termos de norma.

lessons.title: Discutindo normas, conformidade e auditorias externas com a AWS
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você discute normas, conformidade e auditorias externas com a AWS, aplicando em conversa os modais de obrigação de segunda e defendendo a cultura de segurança da Racional como diferencial.
lessons.overview:
Today is the construction site: you talk to AWS about the most sensitive topic of the safety pillar — compliance and external audits. For Amazon/AWS, a construction partner needs to prove, with documents and certifications, that it does everything it says. There is no new theory: you will use, by speaking, the verbs of obligation you studied on Monday.

You will practice how to defend Racional with firmness and warmth. You can say that the company fully complies with all standards, that it is certified and that it keeps a clear audit trail. And you can go further: show that Racional not only meets but seeks to go beyond and exceed the standard, opening the doors with a cordial you're welcome to check.

This is where the safety culture becomes a sale. You close by positioning safety as something non-negotiable and as a true differentiator for Racional in front of AWS. The weight of the lesson is on speaking with the teacher: defending, under questions, what makes the company trustworthy.
lessons.intro:
Sem teoria nova: vamos defender a Racional na conversa. Retome de segunda "comply with", "required to" e "mandatory" e use-os para falar de auditoria.

Frases-âncora para o role-play: "We fully comply with every standard.", "You're welcome to audit our site." e "For us, safety is non-negotiable."
lessons.situation: Reunião com a AWS sobre conformidade. O cliente pergunta sobre normas e auditorias externas, e você defende a cultura de segurança da Racional como diferencial.
lessons.context: Thank you for the question. We fully comply with every standard. We are certified, and we are happy to show our audit trail. You're welcome to send an external auditor to our site any time. We don't just meet the requirements; we go beyond them. We want to exceed the standard, not only follow it. For us, safety is non-negotiable. This is what makes us in line with your needs, and this is our real differentiator.

We go beyond the basic rules.
We want to exceed the standard.
We meet every requirement.
We keep a clear audit trail.

We are in line with your needs.

Safety is our real differentiator.

lessons.title: Past tenses na narrativa de eventos e ações (relato de incidentes)
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você saberá narrar um incidente ou quase-acidente da obra usando o Past Simple para o fato e o Past Continuous para o cenário, sem trocar o tempo verbal no meio do relato.
lessons.overview:
Reporting safety is, above all, telling what happened in a clear and ordered way. In Racional's daily routine, every site event — an incident or a near miss — becomes a short account that must be understood by engineers and by clients alike. In the monthly meetings with Microsoft, Amazon/AWS and Google, that account in English is what shows control and maturity of the operation.

A good account always follows the same blueprint: the scenario (what was happening), the event (what occurred) and the action taken. Who noticed the hazard, who decided to stop the activity, and how the team acted immediately. This fixed order makes the account easy to follow and impossible to misread — exactly what a big tech expects from a supplier.

This lesson is the blueprint of the language for that. You will study two tenses: the Past Simple, for the completed fact ("a worker reported the hazard"), and the Past Continuous, for the background ("the team was working when..."). Mastering the switch from one to the other is what separates a confusing account from a professional one. On Friday, you will use this structure live with the client.
lessons.intro:
Hoje fixamos a regra que sexta vira fala. Duas frases-âncora sustentam todo o relato:

Past Continuous (was/were + verbo-ing) = o cenário: "The team was installing the panels...". Past Simple = o fato e a ação: "...when a worker noticed a hazard. He stopped the activity immediately."
lessons.situation: Você prepara, por escrito e em voz baixa, o relato de um quase-acidente da obra do data center, para apresentá-lo na reunião mensal com a Microsoft.
lessons.context: Last Tuesday, the team was installing electrical panels on the third floor. While they were working, a worker noticed a loose cable. He stopped the activity immediately and reported the hazard. Nobody got hurt, and we fixed the problem in one hour.

vocab.example: We had one small incident last month.
The near miss was reported the same day.
The worker saw a hazard on the scaffold.
The event occurred during the night shift.
A supervisor noticed the loose cable.
We stopped the activity right away.
He reported the hazard immediately.
Nobody got hurt in the event.
We fixed the problem in one hour.
It happened during the day shift.
The team was checking the scaffold.
We acted immediately.
While they were working, the alarm sounded.
We took action on the same day.

exercises.title: 1. Cenário ou fato?
exercises.prompt: Para o cenário em andamento (o que estava acontecendo), qual forma está certa? "The team ___ the panels when the alarm sounded."

options.whyWrong: 'Installed' é Past Simple (fato pontual). O pano de fundo em andamento pede Past Continuous: 'was installing'.
'Is installing' é presente. O relato é no passado: use 'was installing'.

exercises.explanation: Cenário em andamento no passado = Past Continuous (was/were + -ing). O evento que o interrompe vem no Past Simple.

exercises.title: 2. O fato concluído
exercises.prompt: A worker ___ (notice) the loose cable and stopped the activity.
exercises.explanation: 'Notice' é regular: notice + -d. A ação concluída do relato vai no Past Simple.

commonErrors.notice: Faltou o passado. Para um fato concluído, use 'noticed'.
commonErrors.was noticing: Aqui é o fato pontual, não o cenário; use o Past Simple 'noticed'.

exercises.title: 3. Monte a frase do evento
exercises.explanation: Sujeito (He) + verbo no Past Simple (stopped) + objeto (the activity) + advérbio (immediately). A ação tomada fecha o relato.

exercises.title: 4. Combine a forma com o uso

pairs.right: marca o que estava em andamento

exercises.explanation: 'When' acompanha o evento (Past Simple); 'while' acompanha o pano de fundo (Past Continuous). São os dois marcadores que organizam o relato.

exercises.title: 5. Seu mini-relato (cenário + evento)
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases sobre um quase-acidente: (1) o cenário no Past Continuous e (2) o evento e a ação no Past Simple. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta lição. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: While the team was installing the panels, a worker noticed a hazard on the scaffold. He stopped the activity immediately and reported the near miss, and nobody got hurt.
exercises.explanation: Cenário (Past Continuous) + evento e resposta (Past Simple) = a estrutura completa de um relato em duas frases.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em cerca de 15 segundos, narre um incidente ou quase-acidente real da sua obra: comece pelo cenário (was/were + -ing) e marque o evento e a ação tomada no Past Simple. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can describe the background of an event with the past continuous.
I can say what happened with the past simple.
I can link the scene and the event with 'while' and 'when'.
I can report a near miss without mixing past and present.
I can end the report with the action we took.

lessons.title: Incident reporting & lessons learned a um cliente big tech
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você saberá relatar um incidente e suas lições aprendidas a um cliente big tech numa conversa, mostrando controle, transparência e o que mudou depois.
lessons.overview:
Reporting an incident to a big tech is not confessing a failure — it is proving maturity. The client does not judge Racional by the event; it judges by the reaction to the event. That is why every account ends with the lessons learned: what the company did so that it does not happen again. In a meeting with Amazon/AWS, this closing matters more than the safety number itself.

The path is always the same: investigate the root cause, take the corrective action, update the checklist and follow up. You stay transparent and show that the team acted promptly. This vocabulary turns a problem into proof of process.

This is the practice lesson: no new theory. You pick up Monday's past tenses and use them in a real conversation with the teacher. We will simulate the Amazon account manager asking about the month's safety indicators — and you answering with the complete account: fact, cause, action and the phrase that reassures the client: "it won't happen again".
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora para a simulação de hoje:

"Last month, we had one near miss." (abre com o fato) · "We investigated the root cause and took corrective action." (resposta) · "No one was injured, and we made sure it won't happen again." (fechamento que tranquiliza).
lessons.situation: Na reunião mensal com a Amazon/AWS, o gerente de conta pergunta sobre os indicadores de segurança do mês. Você relata um quase-acidente e o que a Racional aprendeu com ele.
lessons.context: Last month, we had one near miss on site. The team was checking the scaffold when a supervisor noticed a missing safety pin. We stopped the work immediately and investigated the root cause. No one was injured. As a lesson learned, we updated our checklist, so it won't happen again.

vocab.example: Let me share the lessons learned from last month.
We investigated the root cause.
The root cause was a missing check.
No one was injured in the event.
We updated the checklist after the event.
The checklist is now mandatory.
We take every near miss seriously.
The corrective action took two days.
These steps prevent a repeat event.
We made sure it won't happen again.
We stay transparent with our clients on safety.
We followed up on every action.
We addressed the issue the same day.
The team responded promptly.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva o fechamento do relato
exercises.correctText: We investigated the root cause and took corrective action.
exercises.explanation: Esta é a frase que mostra controle ao cliente: causa-raiz primeiro, ação corretiva depois. Decore o ritmo dela.

exercises.title: 2. Monte a frase que tranquiliza o cliente
exercises.explanation: "We made sure it won't happen again" é o fechamento que transforma o incidente em prova de aprendizado. Use-a no fim do relato.

exercises.title: 3. Relate o quase-acidente em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Last month, we had one near miss. We investigated the root cause, took corrective action, and updated our checklist. No one was injured.
exercises.translation: No mês passado, tivemos um quase-acidente. Investigamos a causa-raiz, tomamos ação corretiva e atualizamos nossa lista de verificação. Ninguém ficou ferido.
exercises.prompt: Você é o Fábio na reunião com a Amazon. Relate o evento com calma, marcando bem fato, ação e fechamento.
exercises.explanation: Fale como quem está no controle: fato no passado, ação no passado, e o alívio de 'no one was injured'. Repita até soar natural.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em cerca de 20 segundos, relate ao gerente da Amazon um incidente da sua obra: abra com o fato, explique a ação corretiva e a lição aprendida, e feche dizendo que não vai se repetir. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can open a safety report with the fact, not an excuse.
I can explain the root cause and the corrective action.
I can say that no one was injured.
I can close with the lesson learned.
I can tell the client it won't happen again.
