lessons.title: Estrutura de programa: descrevendo "Tô Sabendo", DSM, treinamentos
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você saberá descrever a estrutura de um programa de segurança — o que é, como funciona e para que serve — usando o Present Simple e o conector de finalidade 'to + verbo' / 'so that'.
lessons.overview:
Describing a program is different from narrating an event. Here you do not talk about the past, but about something that exists and works every week. Racional brings three programs to every project: the DSM, a daily safety dialogue; 'To Sabendo', which shares lessons from real cases; and the training that keeps the team certified. Knowing how to explain them in English is showing the big tech that safety here is routine, not a slogan.

For Google and the other clients, what impresses is not the name of the program, but its purpose: each one exists to raise awareness, ensure compliance and engage the worker. Describing this well turns three internal acronyms into a management differentiator that is visible to whoever audits the project.

This lesson is the blueprint of the language for that description. You will lock in the Present Simple (verb with -s in the third person: "the program covers...", "it includes...") and the connector of purpose. The golden rule: for each program, answer three questions in order — what it is, how it works, why it matters. On Friday, this becomes a sales argument.
lessons.intro:
Hoje fixamos a tríade que descreve qualquer programa:

"The DSM is a daily safety dialogue." (o que é) · "Each team holds it before the shift." (como funciona) · "We run it to raise awareness, so that everyone knows the risks." (para quê serve).
lessons.situation: Você prepara, por escrito, a explicação dos programas de segurança da Racional — 'Tô Sabendo', DSM e treinamentos — para apresentá-los ao Google na próxima reunião.
lessons.context: We run three safety programs on every site. The DSM is a daily safety dialogue: each team holds a short talk before the shift to review the day's risks. The 'Tô Sabendo' program shares lessons from real cases, so that workers learn from past events. We also provide regular training to keep everyone certified and aware.

vocab.example: We run three safety programs on site.
The program consists of three parts.
It includes a daily talk and training.
The DSM is a daily safety dialogue.
We run it to raise awareness.
The talk keeps everyone aware of the risks.
We provide regular training on site.
Training certifies every new worker.
These programs ensure compliance with the rules.
The checklist ensures a safe start.
We engage every team in safety.
We run training regularly.
We share cases so that workers learn.
The purpose is to keep everyone safe.

exercises.title: 1. Programa é 'it': qual verbo?
exercises.prompt: Falando de um programa (terceira pessoa), qual forma está certa? "The DSM ___ a short talk before the shift."

options.whyWrong: Falta o -s da terceira pessoa. O programa é 'it', então: 'includes'.
Não se usa 'is' antes do verbo principal. O Present Simple na terceira pessoa é só 'includes'.

exercises.explanation: Programa = 'it' = verbo com -s no Present Simple: includes, covers, helps, keeps.

exercises.title: 2. O conector de finalidade
exercises.prompt: We share real cases ___ ___ workers learn from past events.
exercises.explanation: 'So that' liga a ação ao seu propósito: fazemos X para que Y aconteça.

commonErrors.for that: Não existe 'for that' nesse sentido; use 'so that'.
commonErrors.to that: Para ligar a uma oração com sujeito e verbo, use 'so that'.

exercises.title: 3. Monte a frase do propósito
exercises.explanation: Sujeito + verbo + objeto + finalidade com 'to + verbo'. "We run it to raise awareness" responde à pergunta 'para quê?'.

exercises.title: 4. Combine o programa com seu propósito

pairs.right: daily safety dialogue before the shift
to raise awareness and ensure compliance

exercises.explanation: Cada programa tem uma função clara. Saber ligar nome a propósito é o que torna a descrição convincente.

exercises.title: 5. Descreva um programa em 2 frases
exercises.prompt: Descreva um programa de segurança da Racional: (1) o que é / o que faz e (2) para que serve. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta lição. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: The DSM is a daily safety dialogue before every shift. We run it to raise awareness, so that the whole team knows the risks of the day.
exercises.explanation: O que é (Present Simple) + para que serve (to + verbo / so that) = a descrição completa de um programa.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em cerca de 15 segundos, descreva o DSM ou o 'Tô Sabendo' para um auditor do Google: diga o que é, como funciona e para que serve. Mantenha tudo no presente. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can describe a safety program in the present simple.
I can say what a program is and what it does.
I can explain its purpose with 'to' and 'so that'.
I can use the -s on the verb when I talk about the program.
I can present our programs as a real routine, not a slogan.

lessons.title: Defendendo a cultura de segurança da Racional como diferencial
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você saberá defender a cultura de segurança da Racional como diferencial competitivo numa conversa com cliente big tech, ligando cada resultado de segurança a um ganho do cliente.
lessons.overview:
For a big tech, safety is not a cost — it is continuity of operation, reputation and trust. A project that stops because of an accident delays the client's data center. That is why Racional's safety culture stops being a compliance item and becomes a competitive advantage: it is what makes the company set us apart among the suppliers of Google, Amazon and Microsoft.

The secret to defending this well is never to leave a number standing alone. Each indicator — a strong track record, millions of hours with zero lost-time incident — needs to be connected to a benefit for whoever is listening: "this protects your reputation", "you can count on us". It is your safety turning into a business argument, with the calm the client is looking for: peace of mind.

This is the practice lesson: with no new theory, you combine the past tenses (the results we delivered) and the Present Simple (how we work) from the module's theory lessons. We will simulate a conversation with Google about supplier reliability — and you positioning Racional as the company that walks the talk.

Frases-âncora para a simulação de hoje:

"At Racional, safety comes first." (o princípio) · "Last year, we worked millions of hours with zero lost-time incidents." (a prova) · "This protects your schedule and your reputation. You can count on us." (o ganho do cliente).

lessons.title: Mapa dos tempos verbais: passado, presente e futuro lado a lado
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você saberá enxergar passado, presente e futuro lado a lado num único mapa e escolher o tempo verbal certo pelo marcador de tempo, sem misturar os tempos no meio da frase.
lessons.overview:
In the monthly report meetings with Microsoft, what you say always falls into three boxes: what has already been done, what is in progress and what comes next. A clear status update depends on putting each sentence in the right tense — and your biggest sticking point, raised in your interview, is precisely switching the tense in the middle of speaking. This lesson fixes that once and for all.

The blueprint is simple: past for what is finished ("last month, we completed the foundation"), present for the status right now ("the project is on schedule") and future for what is still to come ("next month, we will begin the installation"). Each box has its guide words: the project timeline, the current phase, what is underway and what is upcoming.

This is the blueprint of the language for your verb-tense axis. The golden rule is the time marker: it decides the verb. "Last week" calls for the past; "at the moment" calls for the present; "next month" calls for the future. Find the marker first and keep the tense until the full stop. On Friday, you will do this live on a call with the client.
lessons.intro:
Hoje fixamos a régua dos três tempos pelo marcador:

"Last month, we completed the foundation." (passado) · "At the moment, the structure is on schedule." (presente) · "Next month, we will begin the installation." (futuro). Ache o marcador, e o verbo segue.
lessons.situation: Você prepara a estrutura da sua call mensal de status com a Microsoft: o que já foi feito, o que está em curso e o que vem a seguir.
lessons.context: Last month, we completed the foundation works. At the moment, the structure is on schedule and the team is fully mobilized. Next month, we will begin the electrical installation. So we are exactly where we planned to be.

The project is on schedule.

exercises.title: 1. O marcador decide o tempo
exercises.prompt: Qual verbo combina com o marcador? "Next month, we ___ the electrical installation."

options.whyWrong: 'Completed' é passado. 'Next month' aponta para o futuro: use 'will begin'.
Para um plano futuro com 'next month', use o futuro com 'will': 'will begin'.

exercises.explanation: Marcador 'next month' = futuro = will + verbo. Ache o marcador primeiro; o verbo segue.

exercises.title: 2. O status de agora
exercises.prompt: At the moment, the structure ___ (be) on schedule.
exercises.explanation: 'At the moment' pede o presente. O status atual usa o Present Simple: 'is on schedule'.

commonErrors.was: 'At the moment' é agora, não passado; use 'is'.
commonErrors.will be: O status atual é presente, não futuro; use 'is'.

exercises.title: 3. Monte a frase do passado concluído
exercises.explanation: Marcador no início (Last month) + sujeito + verbo no passado (completed) + objeto. O marcador abre a frase e fixa o tempo.

exercises.title: 4. Combine o marcador com o tempo verbal
exercises.explanation: Cada marcador puxa um tempo. Treinar esse pareamento é o que evita a troca de tempo no meio da fala.

exercises.title: 5. Três frases, três tempos
exercises.prompt: Escreva 3 frases sobre uma obra: uma no passado, uma no presente e uma no futuro, cada uma com seu marcador. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta lição. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
keywords: at the moment|on schedule|underway|phase|next month|upcoming|will begin
exercises.modelAnswer: Last month, we completed the foundation. At the moment, the structure is on schedule. Next month, we will begin the electrical phase.
exercises.explanation: Um tempo por caixa, cada um com seu marcador. Essa é a régua que organiza o status update.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em cerca de 15 segundos, dê um mini status de uma obra com três frases: o que terminou (passado), onde está agora (presente) e o que vem (futuro). Use um marcador em cada frase. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can place each sentence in the right tense by the time marker.
I can use the past for what is done.
I can use the present for the current status.
I can use the future for the next steps.
I can keep one tense from start to end of the sentence.

lessons.title: Status update mensal: escolhendo o tempo verbal certo ao vivo
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você saberá conduzir um status update mensal ao vivo, escolhendo o tempo verbal certo na hora — passado para o que terminou, presente para o status e futuro para o que vem.
lessons.overview:
Today is the construction site, not the blueprint. Every monthly meeting with Microsoft opens with the same question: "So, where do we stand?". From there, you lead an entire status update — and the challenge is just one: keeping each sentence in the right tense while you speak, live, with no script in front of you.

The structure is fixed and in your favor: what happened since our last call, where we are now, and what comes looking ahead. Anchor phrases mark each turn: you say "to give an update", report what happened in the inspection, confirm that you are on target and close with the next steps. Each anchor forces you to change the verb along with it.

This is the practice lesson: with no new theory, you use Monday's map of tenses in a simulated call with the Microsoft account manager. The executive tip is to announce the tense change out loud — when you say "looking ahead", the client already knows the future is coming, and you force yourself to use "will". Today's weight is on speaking with the teacher.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora para a call de hoje, uma por bloco de tempo:

"Since our last call, we completed the foundation." (passado) · "At the moment, the site is fully staffed." (presente) · "Looking ahead, we will start the electrical works." (futuro).
lessons.situation: Call mensal de status com o gerente de conta da Microsoft. Ele abre com "So, where do we stand?" e espera de você um panorama claro em passado, presente e futuro.
lessons.context: Thanks, James. Let me give you a quick update. Since our last call, we completed the foundation and passed the inspection. At the moment, we are building the steel structure and the site is fully staffed. Looking ahead, we will start the electrical works in July. Overall, we are right on target.

vocab.example: Since our last call, we completed two steps.
Let me show you where we stand.
Let me give you a quick update.
We passed the inspection last week.
Looking ahead, we will start the next phase.
The site is fully staffed now.
Overall, we are on target.
The main highlight is the inspection result.
We are on target for July.
I want to flag one small delay.
Here are the next steps.
Let me recap the main points.
To date, we have no incidents.
The work is going smoothly.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva a âncora do passado
exercises.correctText: Since our last call, we completed the foundation and passed the inspection.
exercises.explanation: Esta âncora abre o bloco do passado. 'Since our last call' avisa o cliente: o que vem agora já aconteceu.

exercises.title: 2. Monte a âncora do futuro
exercises.explanation: "Looking ahead" abre o bloco do futuro e te obriga a usar 'will'. Anuncie a virada e o verbo segue.

exercises.title: 3. Conduza o status update em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Let me give you a quick update. Since our last call, we completed the foundation. At the moment, the site is fully staffed. Looking ahead, we will start the electrical works.
exercises.translation: Deixe-me dar uma atualização rápida. Desde nossa última call, concluímos a fundação. No momento, a obra está com a equipe completa. Olhando adiante, vamos começar a parte elétrica.
exercises.prompt: Você é o Fábio na call com a Microsoft. Conduza o update inteiro, anunciando cada troca de tempo em voz alta.
exercises.explanation: Marque bem as três âncoras: 'since our last call', 'at the moment', 'looking ahead'. Cada uma muda o verbo junto.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, em cerca de 20 segundos, conduza um status update para o gerente da Microsoft: o que foi feito desde a última call, onde está agora e o que vem a seguir. Anuncie cada troca de tempo. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can open a status update with a clear phrase.
I can report what is done with 'since our last call'.
I can give the current status in the present.
I can announce the next steps with 'looking ahead'.
I can switch tense out loud and keep the call clear.

lessons.title: Present perfect vs. past simple: o que mudou × o que aconteceu
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai separar com clareza o present perfect (o que mudou e vale agora) do past simple (o que aconteceu num momento fechado) para abrir um report com força.
lessons.overview:
A report meeting is the moment when the operations director shows what the project has already delivered and what it is still going to deliver. For this, English uses two different pasts, and this is the foundation of all of Module 6. The present perfect shows a result that still counts today; the past simple tells an event that is finished, with a date. Knowing which one to use changes the strength of your sentence in front of Microsoft, Amazon and Google.

In Racional's daily routine, this comes up all the time. When you say that the company has delivered more than 620 projects in 50 years, you are talking about a living history, a track record that weighs now, at the table. When you say that you finished the foundation in March, you nail down a closed event, with a date. The big-data client wants to hear both things: the accumulated solidity and the precise fact.

This lesson is the blueprint of the language: first the rule, then Friday's practice. The most common mistake of the Brazilian executive is to mix the two, because in Portuguese everything becomes the past. Here you will learn the simple test to choose the right tense and never again put a closed date in the present perfect.
lessons.intro:
Guarde duas frases-âncora para a prática de sexta: "We have delivered more than six hundred projects" (resultado que vale agora) e "We completed the foundation in March" (evento com data).

O teste é simples: se cabe "when?" com uma data, use o past simple. Se a ideia é "o que já temos até agora", use o present perfect. Marcadores como so far, already, yet, just puxam o present perfect.
lessons.situation: Você estrutura a abertura do report mensal para a Microsoft: o que a Racional já conquistou (resultado vivo) e quando bateu cada marco específico.
lessons.context: Over the years, we have delivered more than six hundred projects in Brazil. We have already completed two phases of this data center, and we have had no safety incidents so far. We finished the foundation in March, and we passed the inspection last week. Our track record is strong, and we are proud of it.

vocab.example: We have had no incidents so far.
We have already completed two phases.
We have not started the testing yet.
We have just passed the inspection.
We have achieved a strong safety record.
We have a solid track record.
We have delivered many big projects.
We have worked with them for ten years.
We have been a partner since 2015.
We completed the foundation in March.
The outcome is a safe, ready building.
We have maintained zero incidents.
We have reached two milestones already.
We have more than fifty years of experience.

exercises.title: 1. Resultado que vale agora
exercises.prompt: Você quer mostrar um resultado acumulado que conta hoje, sem dizer quando. Qual frase escolher?

options.text: We delivered more than six hundred projects.
options.whyWrong: O past simple foca um evento fechado. Aqui a ideia é o resultado que ainda vale agora, e isso pede present perfect.

options.text: We have delivered more than six hundred projects.
We have delivered six hundred projects in 1971.
options.whyWrong: Data fechada ('in 1971') não combina com present perfect. Tire a data ou use o past simple.

exercises.title: 2. Evento com data
exercises.prompt: We ___ (finish) the foundation in March.
exercises.explanation: 'In March' é um momento fechado, então use o past simple 'finished'. Data específica nunca vai no present perfect.

commonErrors.have finished: 'Have finished' não aceita a data 'in March'. Com data fechada, use 'finished'.
commonErrors.finish: 'Finish' é presente; o evento já ocorreu em março.

exercises.title: 3. Monte uma frase de resultado
exercises.explanation: Sujeito (We) + have + already + particípio (completed) + complemento. 'Already' fica entre 'have' e o particípio.

exercises.title: 4. Combine o marcador com o tempo verbal

pairs.right: o que já temos até hoje

exercises.explanation: Os marcadores dividem as águas: 'so far / already' puxam o present perfect; datas fechadas puxam o past simple.

exercises.title: 5. Abertura de credibilidade (2 frases)
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases para abrir um report: (1) um resultado acumulado da Racional no present perfect e (2) um marco específico com data no past simple. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta lição. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
keywords: have delivered|have achieved|have maintained|so far|already|track record
exercises.modelAnswer: We have delivered more than six hundred projects, and we have maintained a strong safety record so far. We completed the foundation of this data center in March and reached our second milestone last week.
exercises.explanation: Resultado acumulado (present perfect) mais evento datado (past simple): essa dupla abre o report com credibilidade e precisão.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, diga uma conquista da Racional que vale até hoje (present perfect) e um marco específico com a data em que aconteceu (past simple). Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can use the present perfect for results that still matter now.
I can use the past simple for finished events with a date.
I can avoid putting a closed date in the present perfect.
I can open a report with our track record and a dated milestone.

lessons.title: Report de progresso de obra para a Microsoft
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai apresentar o progresso de uma obra à Microsoft escolhendo ao vivo entre present perfect (o que já entregamos) e past simple (o que aconteceu, com data).
lessons.overview:
The progress report is one of the most important meetings for an operations director. It is where the big-data client hears how far the project has advanced, which milestones were hit and how safety is going on site. Microsoft, owner of critical data centers, follows every percentage and every deadline closely. Reporting well in English conveys control and confidence.

In Racional's routine, a good report mixes the two pasts you structured on Monday. You start with the living accumulated total: the project has completed sixty percent of the structure and has stayed on budget so far. Then you go down to the dated milestones: you poured the slab in May and passed the safety audit last week. Safety goes back to the present perfect: we have had zero accidents so far.

Today there is no new theory. It is the construction site: you will simulate the report live with the teacher, in the role of operations director talking to the Microsoft account manager. The focus is on speaking, training the switch between the two tenses until it sounds natural, with the result always coming ahead of the dated detail.
lessons.intro: Frases-âncora para a simulação: "We have completed about sixty percent of the structure" (acumulado), "We poured the main slab in May" (marco datado) e "We have had zero incidents so far" (segurança).
lessons.situation: Reunião mensal de progresso de obra com a Microsoft. O gerente de conta quer saber quanto avançou, quais marcos foram batidos e como está a segurança no canteiro.
lessons.context: Here is where we are on the build. We have completed about sixty percent of the structure, and we have stayed on budget so far. We poured the main slab in May, and we passed the safety audit last week. On safety, we have had zero lost-time incidents since the project started. The next pour is scheduled for June.

vocab.example: Let me walk you through the progress report.
We have stayed on budget so far.
We poured the main slab in May.
The main slab is now complete.
We passed the safety audit last week.
We have had zero lost-time incidents.
The structure is sixty percent complete.
We stayed within the planned cost.
We are in full compliance with the rules.
The next pour is scheduled for June.
The headcount on site is two hundred.
We have hit every target so far.
We had no rework on this phase.
Here is where we are on the build.

exercises.title: 1. Ouça e escreva o acumulado
exercises.correctText: We have completed sixty percent of the structure so far.
exercises.explanation: Acumulado vivo no present perfect, com o marcador 'so far'. Esse é o tom de abertura do report.

exercises.title: 2. Ouça e escreva o marco datado
exercises.correctText: We poured the main slab in May.
exercises.explanation: Past simple com data fechada ('in May'). Quando o cliente pergunta 'when?', a resposta vem aqui.

exercises.title: 3. Monte o placar de segurança
exercises.explanation: Present perfect para o resultado de segurança que vale hoje: We + have + had + complemento + so far.

exercises.title: 4. Monte o acumulado da obra
exercises.explanation: Acumulado no present perfect: We + have + completed + a quantidade. Foco no total até agora.

exercises.title: 5. Apresente o progresso ao vivo
exercises.targetText: We have completed about sixty percent of the structure. We poured the main slab in May, and we have had zero incidents so far.
exercises.translation: Concluímos cerca de sessenta por cento da estrutura. Concretamos a laje principal em maio, e tivemos zero acidentes até agora.
exercises.prompt: Leia em voz alta como se estivesse reportando o progresso à Microsoft agora. Resultado primeiro, fato datado depois.
exercises.explanation: Acumulado no present perfect, marco no past simple, segurança no present perfect. Treine a troca até soar natural.

exercises.title: 6. Feche com o próximo passo
exercises.targetText: We have stayed on budget, and the next pour is scheduled for June.
exercises.translation: Ficamos dentro do orçamento, e a próxima concretagem está agendada para junho.
exercises.prompt: Leia em voz alta fechando o report: o resultado de custo e o próximo evento agendado.
exercises.explanation: Resultado de orçamento no present perfect e próximo passo com 'scheduled for'. Esse fechamento passa controle.

lessons.critical: Em 20 segundos, reporte o progresso de uma obra sua à Microsoft: quanto já avançou (present perfect), um marco com data (past simple) e a segurança até hoje (present perfect). Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can report cumulative progress with the present perfect.
I can anchor a dated milestone with the past simple.
I can present a safety record with 'we have had zero incidents so far'.
I can switch between the two past tenses live in a progress report.

lessons.title: Os futuros do report: will, going to, present continuous, future perfect
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai escolher o futuro certo do report: will (decisão/promessa), going to (plano), present continuous (agendado) e future perfect (estará pronto até uma data).
lessons.overview:
In English there is not just one future: there are four, and each says something different. For an operations director who lives by deadlines, choosing the right future is choosing the level of commitment you take on in front of Amazon, Google or Microsoft. This is the blueprint of the futures, the basis of the deadline projections in all of Module 6.

In Racional's practice, this comes up when talking about upcoming milestones. The will (future of decision) is the direct promise: "We will send the schedule by Friday". The going to (decided plan) shows firm intention: "We are going to start the commissioning". The present continuous marks what is already scheduled: "We are meeting the inspectors on Tuesday". And the future perfect projects a milestone already completed by a certain date: "By Q3, we will have energized the building".

This lesson is Monday's theory: first the rule, then Friday's practice with AWS. The strong negotiation point is the future perfect with "by": saying that by December the structure will have been completed sounds much more planned and firm than a simple "we will complete". That is the future that conveys control of the schedule.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora para a prática: "We are going to start the commissioning in July" (plano), "We will send the schedule by Friday" (promessa) e "By Q3, we will have completed the installation" (marco pronto até a data).

Regra de ouro: para projeção de prazo, prefira o future perfect com "by". Ele projeta o marco já entregue dentro do prazo.
lessons.situation: Você prepara a parte de projeções do report para a AWS: o que vai começar, o que já está agendado e quais marcos estarão concluídos até cada trimestre.
lessons.context: Let me walk you through what is next. We are going to start the commissioning phase in July. We are meeting the energy provider next Tuesday to confirm the connection. We will send you the updated schedule by Friday. And by the third quarter, we will have completed the full electrical installation.

vocab.example: We are going to start in July.
The commissioning phase starts in July.
We are meeting them to confirm the date.
We will send the report by Friday.
By Q3, we will have energized the building.
Here is our projection for the quarter.
Our forecast is on track.
The handover is on the agenda.
We are starting the next phase.
We are going to roll out the plan in August.
Completion is planned for December.
We anticipate no delays.
The handover is scheduled for Q4.
The report is due on Friday.

exercises.title: 1. Marco pronto até uma data
exercises.prompt: Você quer projetar que a instalação estará concluída até o terceiro trimestre. Qual frase usar?

options.whyWrong: É correto, mas não projeta o marco pronto dentro de um prazo. Para isso, use o future perfect com 'by'.

options.text: By Q3, we will have completed the installation.
We are completing the installation by Q3.
options.whyWrong: O present continuous serve para algo agendado, não para projetar um marco concluído até uma data. Use o future perfect.

exercises.title: 2. Plano já decidido
exercises.prompt: We ___ start the commissioning phase in July.
exercises.explanation: Plano firme e já decidido pede 'going to': we are going to start. Mostra intenção planejada, não decisão na hora.

commonErrors.will: 'Will' soa como decisão de momento; aqui o plano já está fechado, então use 'going to'.
commonErrors.are go to: A forma correta é 'are going to' + verbo no infinitivo.

exercises.title: 3. Monte uma promessa de prazo
exercises.explanation: Promessa direta com 'will': We + will + verbo + complemento + by + prazo. 'By Friday' marca o limite.

exercises.title: 4. Combine o futuro com o seu uso
exercises.explanation: Cada futuro marca um nível de compromisso. O future perfect com 'by' é o mais forte para projeção de prazo.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, faça uma projeção de prazo para a AWS: um plano com going to e um marco que estará concluído até uma data com future perfect. Sem texto na frente.

I can use 'going to' for a plan that is already decided.

I can use the future perfect with 'by' to project a finished milestone.

lessons.title: Projeções e próximos marcos com a AWS ("by Q3 we will have…")
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai apresentar projeções e próximos marcos à AWS escolhendo ao vivo o futuro certo, com destaque para o future perfect ('by Q3 we will have...').
lessons.overview:
Every data center project lives on milestones: key dates that the client follows closely. For AWS, each finished data hall means revenue, so the projections part of the report is the one that carries the most weight. Knowing how to commit to a date in English, in the right tone, is what separates a reliable supplier from one who stalls.

In Racional's routine, this means lock a date, mobilize the team and commit to a date without promising what cannot be delivered. Here you use the four futures from Monday, with weight on the future perfect: "By Q3, we will have delivered the first data hall". It is the sentence that places the finished milestone within the quarter and shows that the project is on track.

Today there is no new theory. It is the construction site: you will simulate with the teacher the projections part of a report for AWS, in the role of operations director. The focus is on speaking, locking in the deadline-commitment sentence and training the firm but realistic tone when closing a date with the client.
lessons.intro: Frases-âncora para a simulação: "By the end of Q3, we will have delivered the first data hall" (marco pronto até a data), "We are on track for the September go-live" (no caminho) e "We can commit to that date" (assumir o prazo).
lessons.situation: Reunião de projeções com a AWS. O cliente quer marcos firmes: quando o primeiro data hall fica pronto e quando ocorre o go-live.
lessons.context: Let me share our plan for the next quarter. We are on track for the September go-live. By the end of Q3, we will have delivered the first data hall. We are going to mobilize the second team in August. We can lock that date, and we will confirm the full schedule by Friday.

We can lock that date now.

lessons.critical: Em 20 segundos, apresente uma projeção para a AWS: o status atual com 'on track for' e um marco que estará entregue até uma data com future perfect. Sem texto na frente.

lessons.title: Conduzindo a reunião: agenda, action items e linguagem do chair
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conhecer a linguagem de quem conduz a reunião: abrir a agenda, passar a palavra, registrar action items e fechar com os próximos passos.
lessons.overview:
Leading a report meeting is different from just taking part in it. Whoever chairs the meeting opens the agenda, controls the time, hands over the floor and closes with clarity. For an operations director who reports to Microsoft, Amazon and Google, mastering this language shows leadership and organization, no matter how simple the English still is.

This is the blueprint of the meeting, and each piece has a name. The agenda lists the items. You go through each item, hand over to someone and record the action items with their owners. At the end, you do the recap and wrap up with the next steps and the deadlines. The minutes keep everything in writing.

This lesson is Monday's theory: first the standard phrases of whoever leads, then Friday's practice with Google. The goal is to give you a set of ready, short phrases to open, steer and close the meeting firmly, keeping the time under control and making clear who does what and by when.
lessons.intro:
Frases-âncora para a prática: "Let's go through the agenda" (abrir a pauta), "I'll hand over to you" (passar a palavra) e "Let's wrap up with the next steps" (fechar).

Guarde também a frase de tarefa: "The action item is yours, due Friday" (tarefa, responsável e prazo).
lessons.situation: Você estrutura como vai conduzir a reunião mensal de report: abrir a pauta, controlar o tempo, registrar tarefas e fechar com os próximos passos.
lessons.context: Let's get started and go through the agenda. The first item is the build progress. I'll hand over to the site team for the update. Let's keep this on track, because we have three items today. The action item is yours, due next Friday. Let me recap the next steps, and then we will wrap up.

vocab.example: I will chair the meeting today.
The first item on the agenda is safety.
Let's go through the agenda.
I'll hand over to the site team.
Please take the floor.
The action item is due Friday.
Who is the owner of this task?
I will send the minutes by email.
Let's keep this meeting on track.
Let's move on to the next item.
Let me recap the main points.
Let's wrap up with the next steps.
Here are the next steps for the team.
Please send it by Friday.

exercises.title: 1. Passar a palavra
exercises.prompt: Você quer passar a palavra para a equipe de obra dar o update. Qual frase usar?

options.text: I'll hand over to the site team for the update.
I'll move the site team for the update.
options.whyWrong: 'Move' sozinho não passa a palavra. A expressão correta é 'hand over to' alguém.

options.text: I'll wrap up to the site team for the update.
options.whyWrong: 'Wrap up' é encerrar a reunião, não passar a palavra. Use 'hand over to'.

exercises.title: 2. Abrir a pauta
exercises.prompt: Let's ___ the agenda before we start.
exercises.explanation: 'Go through the agenda' é percorrer a pauta no começo da reunião. É a frase de abertura de quem conduz.

commonErrors.go: Falta a preposição: a expressão é 'go through' the agenda.
commonErrors.go to: 'Go to' significa ir a um lugar; para percorrer a pauta, use 'go through'.

exercises.title: 3. Registre a tarefa
exercises.explanation: Tarefa + responsável + prazo: The action item + is yours + due + data. Deixa claro quem faz o quê e até quando.

exercises.title: 4. Combine a fase da reunião com a frase

pairs.right: Let's wrap up with the next steps.

exercises.explanation: Cada fase da reunião tem sua frase pronta. Decorar essas frases dá a você o controle da condução.

exercises.title: 5. Sua abertura e fechamento (2 frases)
exercises.prompt: Escreva 2 frases para conduzir um report: (1) abra a reunião percorrendo a pauta e (2) feche encerrando com os próximos passos. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta lição. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: Let's get started and go through the agenda; we have three items today. At the end, I'll recap the action items and we will wrap up with the next steps.
exercises.explanation: Abertura (go through the agenda) mais fechamento (wrap up with the next steps): é o esqueleto de uma reunião bem conduzida.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, conduza o começo de uma reunião de report: abra a pauta, diga quantos itens há e passe a palavra para a equipe. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can open a meeting and go through the agenda.
I can hand over the floor to a team member.
I can record an action item with an owner and a deadline.
I can wrap up a meeting with the next steps.

lessons.title: Conduzindo uma reunião de report com o Google
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você vai conduzir uma reunião de report com o Google ao vivo: abrir, dar o status, registrar bloqueios e fechar com os próximos passos.
lessons.overview:
The status report with a client like Google brings together everything from Module 6: you lead the meeting, give the progress with the right verb tenses, flag problems and close with clarity. It is the moment when the operations director shows that the project is under control and that nothing important stays hidden.

In Racional's routine, this means saying what is underway, what is on schedule and, honestly, what fell behind and how the team is going to catch up. You flag a blocker without beating around the bush and promise to circle back with the solution. Transparency here builds the long-term trust that the whole program is after.

Today there is no new theory. It is the construction site: you will lead, with the teacher, a complete report meeting with Google, from start to finish, in the role of operations director. The focus is on speaking, bringing together the language of whoever leads with the report's verb tenses and training the firm and transparent tone that closes each item with a clear next step.
lessons.intro: Frases-âncora para a simulação: "Let me give you a quick status update" (abrir o status), "The structure is on schedule" (avanço) e "I need to flag one blocker" (sinalizar problema).
lessons.situation: Reunião mensal de status com o Google. Você conduz: dá o avanço da obra, sinaliza um bloqueio e fecha com os próximos passos.
lessons.context: Let me give you a quick status update. The structure is on schedule, and the electrical phase is underway. We fell behind on one delivery last month, but we have a plan to catch up. I need to flag one blocker: we are waiting on a permit. I will circle back with a date by Friday. Going forward, the next step is the safety audit.

exercises.explanation: Frase de abertura de quem conduz o report. Curta e direta, prepara o cliente para o avanço.

lessons.title: Perguntas difíceis: ganhar tempo, hedging e clarificação
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você consegue enfrentar uma pergunta difícil em reunião sem travar, usando três ferramentas: ganhar tempo, suavizar a resposta (hedging) e pedir clarificação.
lessons.overview:
In every monthly report meeting with Microsoft, Amazon or Google, that unexpected question arrives: a deadline, a cost, a number that is not on the tip of your tongue. What separates the confident executive from the insecure one is not having the answer ready, it is having the structure to respond calmly. This lesson is the blueprint for that structure: three tools you build before you need to use them on Friday's job site.

The first tool is buying time: phrases like That's a good question and Let me think for a second buy you three seconds without sounding lost. The second is hedging (softening / not committing to a hard figure): instead of promising an exact number, you use would / might and adverbs like probably and roughly. The third is clarifying: repeating the question back in your own words to make sure you understood what was asked.

For Racional's operations director, this is contract protection. Committing to "two weeks" under pressure and getting it wrong becomes a schedule problem with the client. Saying It would probably take two weeks, let me come back to you protects your word. This lesson prepares Friday's practice, when you will apply everything live in a multi-client meeting.
lessons.intro:
Guarde três frases-âncora para a prática de sexta: That's a good question, let me think for a second (ganhar tempo), It would probably take about two weeks (hedging com would + probably) e Let me come back to you tomorrow (prometer retorno).

A regra do hedge é simples: would / could / might + verbo transforma uma afirmação dura ("It takes two weeks") numa estimativa segura ("It would take about two weeks").
lessons.situation: Você está estudando, antes da reunião com a Amazon, como responder a uma pergunta de prazo que não consegue cravar na hora. O objetivo é fixar a estrutura.
lessons.context: That's a good question. Let me think for a second. It would probably take about two weeks, but I would need to check with my team. As far as I know, the dates still hold. It also depends on the supplier. Let me double-check and come back to you tomorrow.

vocab.example: That's a good question. Let me think.

vocab.en: Let me think for a second
vocab.example: Let me think for a second, please.
I hedge when I am not sure.
It would probably take two weeks.
Roughly two weeks, more or less.
It would take about ten days.
We might need to check the supplier.

vocab.en: off the top of my head
vocab.example: Off the top of my head, about forty units.
Let me come back to you tomorrow.
I will double-check and confirm.

vocab.en: to put me on the spot
vocab.example: You are putting me on the spot a little!
Bear with me while I check the file.

exercises.title: 1. O hedge que protege
exercises.prompt: Você não tem certeza do prazo. Qual resposta soa profissional sem te prender a um número exato?

options.whyWrong: Cravar 'exactly' sem ter certeza te prende; se errar, vira problema no contrato.

options.text: It would probably take about two weeks.

options.whyWrong: 'I have no idea' soa despreparado. Use um hedge ('would probably... about'), não uma rendição.

exercises.explanation: Hedge = would/might + advérbio (probably, about). Você responde com segurança sem se comprometer cedo demais.

exercises.title: 2. Suavize a estimativa
exercises.prompt: It ___ (take) about two weeks, but I would need to confirm.
exercises.explanation: O modal 'would' (ou 'might/could') transforma uma afirmação dura numa estimativa segura: 'It would take about two weeks'.

commonErrors.takes: 'Takes' é fato/rotina e soa como promessa. Use 'would take' para estimar sem cravar.
commonErrors.will take: 'Will take' soa como compromisso firme; para hedge, 'would take' é mais seguro.

exercises.title: 3. Ganhe tempo com classe
exercises.explanation: "That's a good question" é o filler clássico: você reconhece a pergunta e compra alguns segundos para pensar.

exercises.title: 4. Combine a função com a frase

pairs.right: Let me think for a second.
It would probably take two weeks.
Just to make sure I understand the question.
Let me come back to you tomorrow.

exercises.explanation: Quatro frases prontas cobrem qualquer pergunta difícil: tempo, hedge, clarificação e retorno. Memorize-as.

exercises.title: 5. Sua resposta para a pergunta difícil
exercises.prompt: O cliente perguntou um prazo que você não tem na ponta da língua. Responda em 2 frases: (1) ganhe tempo e (2) dê uma estimativa com hedge, prometendo confirmar. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta lição. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
keywords: good question|let me think|bear with me|off the top of my head
probably|roughly|would take|might need to|come back to you|double-check|it depends on

lessons.title: Lidando com perguntas inesperadas em reunião multicliente
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você lida, em conversação com o cliente, com perguntas inesperadas numa reunião que toca mais de um cliente: ganha tempo, suaviza com hedging e protege informação confidencial.
lessons.overview:
Monday's theory becomes the job site today. In this practice you train your composure: the questions come from where you do not expect them and, sometimes, about a different client than the one on the agenda. With the teacher, you will now use the three anchor phrases, buying time, hedging and clarifying, live and under pressure.

The multi-client scenario has a trap: confidentiality. When Google asks about something that touches Amazon, you answer without revealing what you cannot. The elegant way out is to respond in general terms and offer an alternative: I'd be happy to share our own benchmarks.

For Racional's operations director, being vague with elegance is better than being precise with indiscretion. The hedge here is not weakness, it is protection of both the contract and the relationship. Today the weight is on speaking: you simulate the meeting with the teacher until your answer comes out firm and natural.
lessons.intro: Frases-âncora para a simulação de hoje: That's a fair question, let me make sure I follow you (ganhar tempo e clarificar), In general terms, it would depend on the supplier (responder geral com hedge) e I can't go into another client's figures, but I'd be happy to follow up (proteger a confidencialidade e propor retorno).
lessons.situation: Reunião com o Google em que surge uma pergunta inesperada comparando o seu desempenho com outro projeto (da Amazon). Você responde com firmeza, sem expor informação confidencial.
lessons.context: Client: How does Racional compare to your other clients? You: That's a fair question. Let me make sure I follow you. In general terms, our lead times would depend on the supplier and the scope. I can't go into another client's figures, of course, but I'd be happy to share our own benchmarks and follow up tomorrow.

lessons.title: Supply chain: vocabulário de fornecedores, lead time e procurement
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você domina o vocabulário de supply chain — fornecedores, lead time e procurement — e sabe usar o tempo verbal certo para o que foi pedido, o que está a caminho e o que será necessário.
lessons.overview:
Supply chain is your area, and in English it has a web of terms that come up in every meeting with Microsoft, Amazon or Google. This lesson is the blueprint for that web: we build the vocabulary together with the grammar of the right tense, because a purchase order lives exactly on the axis of time, what was bought, what is in transit and what is going to arrive.

Three pillars organize the vocabulary. Suppliers: supplier, vendor and subcontractor, the people who deliver material and service. Lead time: the time between ordering and receiving. Procurement: the process of buying, with purchase order, quote and to source (to find a supplier).

The grammar of time in supply chain is straightforward: past for the order placed (We placed the order last week), present continuous for what is on the way (The steel is arriving next month) and future for the need (We will need two new suppliers). For the operations director, mastering lead time means mastering the delivery promise, you do not promise what the supplier cannot deliver. This lesson prepares Friday's practice, when you will explain the chain to the client.
lessons.intro:
Guarde estas frases-âncora, uma por tempo verbal: We placed the purchase order last week (passado, o pedido já feito), The steel is arriving next month (presente contínuo, o que está a caminho) e We will need two new suppliers (futuro, a necessidade).

A regra: o lead time é um fato presente e estável, então use o presente simples — The lead time is ten weeks.
lessons.situation: Antes da reunião de sexta, você revisa a situação da cadeia de fornecimento do data center: o que foi pedido, o que está chegando e o que ainda precisa ser comprado.
lessons.context: Let me walk you through the supply chain. Last week, we placed the purchase order for the cooling units. The steel structure is arriving next month, right on time. For the next phase, we will need two new suppliers. The lead time for the generators is about ten weeks, so we have to start the procurement now.

vocab.example: Our main supplier is reliable.
We have three vendors for steel.
The subcontractor starts in May.
The lead time is ten weeks.
Procurement starts this week.
We sent the purchase order today.
We placed the order last week.
We have a quote from the vendor.
We can source the steel locally.
The shipment is in transit now.
The shipment arrives on Monday.
Our inventory is low this month.

Rain can delay the shipment.

options.text: We place the purchase order last week.
options.whyWrong: 'Last week' é passado; o verbo precisa estar no passado: 'placed'.

options.text: We placed the purchase order last week.
We will place the purchase order last week.

exercises.explanation: Pedido já feito = passado simples: 'We placed the order last week.' O marcador 'last week' pede o passado.

commonErrors.are: 'Lead time' é singular (um período), então use 'is', não 'are'.
commonErrors.was: 'Was' é passado; o lead time vale agora, então use o presente 'is'.

exercises.title: 3. O que está a caminho
exercises.explanation: Presente contínuo (is + arriving) para o que está a caminho e já tem data: 'The steel is arriving next month.'

exercises.title: 4. Combine o termo com o significado
exercises.explanation: Quatro termos centrais do supply chain. Memorize-os para a prática de sexta com o cliente.

exercises.title: 5. O status da cadeia em 3 tempos

exercises.modelAnswer: Last week we placed the purchase order for the cooling units. The shipment is in transit now. For the next phase, we will need a new supplier because the lead time is ten weeks.
exercises.explanation: Passado para o pedido + presente contínuo para o que vem + futuro para a necessidade = o status completo da cadeia.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, descreva a cadeia de fornecimento do data center em três tempos: o que você já pediu, o que está chegando e o que ainda vai precisar comprar. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can use the past for an order I already placed: 'We placed the order last week.'
I can use the present continuous for what is arriving: 'The steel is arriving next month.'
I can use the future for what we will need: 'We will need two suppliers.'
I can explain a lead time as a present fact: 'The lead time is ten weeks.'

lessons.title: Discussão de supply chain e cadeia de fornecedores com cliente
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você discute, em conversação com o cliente, a cadeia de fornecedores: explica o lead time, justifica o prazo e negocia uma data de entrega realista.
lessons.overview:
Monday's blueprint becomes the job site today. The client wants to understand why a deadline is what it is, and the answer is almost always in the supply chain. In this practice you use the supply chain as a negotiation argument, with firmness and transparency, simulating the conversation with the teacher.

The logic is simple and powerful: the supplier's lead time justifies your deadline. Instead of promising in the dark, you anchor the date to the reality of the chain: The lead time for the generators is ten weeks, so realistically we can install them by August. If there is a risk, you offer an alternative: If there is a shortage, we could source a backup supplier locally.

For Racional's operations director, explaining the lead time is not an excuse, it is professional management that protects your word and the client's trust, even when Microsoft pushes for a faster delivery. Today the weight is on speaking: you practice until you can negotiate the deadline naturally.
lessons.intro: Frases-âncora para a simulação: Let me be transparent about the lead time (abrir com transparência), The lead time is ten weeks, so realistically we can install them by August (ancorar a data) e If there is a shortage, we could source a backup supplier locally (oferecer alternativa para proteger o prazo).
lessons.situation: Reunião com a Microsoft em que o cliente pressiona por uma entrega mais rápida. Você discute a cadeia de fornecedores e o lead time para chegar a uma data realista e segura.
lessons.context: Client: Can you bring the date forward? You: I understand. Let me be transparent about the supply chain. The lead time for the generators is ten weeks, so realistically we can install them by August. We placed the order last week, and the shipment is in transit. If there is a shortage, we could source a backup supplier locally to protect the deadline.

vocab.example: Can we bring the date forward?
Let me be transparent about the plan.
Realistically, we can deliver by August.
We keep a backup supplier for steel.
We can source locally to save time.
We do this to protect the deadline.

We have a contingency for delays.
I can commit to August, not July.
July is not feasible with this lead time.

exercises.explanation: Ouça e escreva. Esta é a frase-chave da negociação: o lead time justifica a data ('so realistically we can install them by August').

exercises.title: 2. Monte a alternativa que protege o prazo
exercises.explanation: Sujeito (We) + modal 'could' (possibilidade) + verbo (source) + objeto (a backup supplier) + local (locally). O 'could' oferece a alternativa sem se comprometer ainda. Leia em voz alta depois.

exercises.title: 3. Negocie o prazo ao vivo
exercises.targetText: Let me be transparent. The lead time for the generators is ten weeks, so realistically we can install them by August. If there is a shortage, we could source a backup supplier locally.
exercises.translation: Deixe-me ser transparente. O prazo de entrega dos geradores é dez semanas, então realisticamente conseguimos instalá-los até agosto. Se houver falta, poderíamos buscar um fornecedor reserva localmente.
exercises.prompt: Leia em voz alta como se respondesse à pressão por prazo numa reunião com a Microsoft. Transparência, data realista e alternativa.
exercises.explanation: Transparência, data realista e alternativa. Treine com o professor até negociar prazo apoiado no lead time, sem ceder ao que é inviável.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, responda a um cliente que pede a entrega antes do possível: explique o lead time, dê uma data realista e ofereça uma alternativa para proteger o prazo. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can explain a delivery date with the supplier's lead time.
I can be transparent about a constraint without promising the impossible.
I can offer a backup supplier or local sourcing to protect the deadline.
I can negotiate a realistic date instead of an unfeasible one.

lessons.title: E-mail e follow-up executivo: estrutura, tom e tempos verbais
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você domina a estrutura, o tom e os tempos verbais de um e-mail e de um follow-up executivo em inglês: abertura, corpo e fechamento.
lessons.overview:
After every meeting with Microsoft, Amazon or Google comes the email: confirming what was agreed, attaching a document, defining the next steps. The executive email is your word in writing, and that is why it needs a clear structure. This lesson is the blueprint for that structure: opening, body and closing, each part with the right verb tense.

The structure has three parts. Opening: Thank you for the meeting and As we discussed bring back the context. Body: Please find attached the quote and Regarding the schedule deal with the topic. Closing: Next steps, Please let me know and Best regards.

The grammar follows the tenses: past for what was agreed (As we agreed yesterday), present for what is attached (Please find attached) and future for the commitment (I will send the report on Friday). For Racional's operations director, a clear email in the right tone confirms the trust built in the meeting. This lesson prepares Friday's practice, when you will write the minutes and the follow-up.
lessons.intro:
Guarde a estrutura em três frases-âncora: Thank you for the meeting. As we discussed, ... (abertura), Please find attached the quote (corpo) e I will get back to you on Friday. Best regards. (fechamento).

A regra do tempo verbal: passado para o que foi combinado, presente para o anexo e futuro (will) para o que você vai fazer.
lessons.situation: Após a reunião com o Google, você revisa a estrutura de um e-mail de follow-up: abrir agradecendo, confirmar o combinado, anexar a cotação e definir o próximo passo.
lessons.context: Dear Mr. Smith, Thank you for the meeting today. As we discussed, please find attached the quote for the cooling units. Regarding the schedule, I will send the full report on Friday. Please let me know if you have any questions. I will get back to you with the dates next week. Best regards, Fabio.

vocab.example: Thank you for the meeting today.
As we discussed, here is the quote.
As agreed, the date is August.
Please find attached the report.
Regarding the schedule, we are on time.
I confirm the meeting for Monday.
Let me list the next steps.
I will send the report on Friday.
I will get back to you next week.
Please let me know if you agree.
Please reply at your earliest convenience.
Best regards, Fabio.
I will keep you posted on the dates.
Looking forward to your reply.

exercises.title: 1. O tempo certo para o compromisso
exercises.prompt: Você quer prometer, no fechamento do e-mail, que vai enviar o relatório na sexta. Qual frase está correta?

options.text: I send the full report on Friday.
options.whyWrong: Presente simples soa como rotina; para um compromisso futuro, use 'will send'.

options.text: I will send the full report on Friday.
I sent the full report on Friday.
options.whyWrong: 'Sent' é passado; aqui você está prometendo algo no futuro, então use 'will send'.

exercises.explanation: Compromisso futuro = 'will' + verbo: 'I will send the report on Friday.' É a promessa clara que fecha o e-mail.

exercises.title: 2. Retome o que foi combinado
exercises.prompt: ___ we discussed, please find attached the quote.
exercises.explanation: 'As we discussed' (conforme conversamos) retoma o combinado da reunião e dá contexto antes do anexo.

commonErrors.How: 'How we discussed' não existe nesse sentido; a expressão fixa é 'As we discussed'.
commonErrors.Like: Em e-mail formal, use 'As we discussed', não 'Like we discussed'.

exercises.title: 3. Anexe com a frase certa
exercises.explanation: "Please find attached the quote" é a fórmula padrão para anexar um documento em e-mail executivo.

exercises.title: 4. Combine a parte do e-mail com a frase

pairs.right: Thank you for the meeting today.

exercises.explanation: Quatro frases prontas montam o e-mail executivo: abertura, retomada, anexo e fechamento. Memorize-as.

exercises.title: 5. Seu e-mail de follow-up
exercises.prompt: Escreva um e-mail curto de follow-up para o cliente após a reunião: agradeça, retome o combinado, anexe a cotação e prometa um próximo passo. Use ao menos 3 termos em inglês desta lição. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.

I will send|get back to you|Please let me know|Best regards|keep you posted
exercises.modelAnswer: Thank you for the meeting today. As we discussed, please find attached the quote for the cooling units. I will send the full report on Friday. Please let me know if you have any questions. Best regards, Fabio.
exercises.explanation: Abertura (Thank you / As we discussed) + corpo (Please find attached) + fechamento (I will send / Best regards) = um e-mail claro e profissional.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, dite o seu e-mail de follow-up após uma reunião com o Google: agradeça, retome o combinado, mencione o anexo e prometa o próximo passo. Sem texto na frente.

I can attach a document with 'Please find attached the quote'.
I can promise a next step with 'I will send the report on Friday'.
I can close an email with 'Please let me know' and 'Best regards'.

pill.tip: Arrastado (drawl) e o clássico 'y'all' (= you all), com as vogais bem alongadas.
pill.sample: Y'all have a great day now — we'll talk real soon.

lessons.title: Ata, follow-up e fechamento de pendências por escrito
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você escreve e comunica, por escrito, a ata e o follow-up de uma reunião: resume as decisões, define responsáveis e prazos e fecha as pendências.
lessons.overview:
Monday's blueprint becomes the job site today. After every meeting with Microsoft, Amazon or Google, someone needs to record what was decided, who became responsible and by when. That record is the minutes and the follow-up. In this practice you produce that text and communicate it with the teacher, closing the module's cycle of written communication.

The minutes have a lean structure: a summary of what was discussed, the decisions, It was agreed that..., and the open items with an owner and a due date. For each open item you say who the owner is and when it should be finished (to close out).

For Racional's operations director, clear minutes prevent misunderstandings about deadlines and responsibility with the client, what was agreed is written down in black and white. Today the weight is on production: you dictate, assemble and read aloud the sentences of the minutes until they come out naturally.
lessons.intro: Frases-âncora para hoje: It was agreed that the report is due on Friday (registrar a decisão e o prazo), This item is still pending; the owner is Fabio (apontar pendência e responsável) e I will follow up to close out the open items (fechar as pendências).
lessons.situation: Após a reunião mensal com a Amazon, você escreve a ata e o follow-up: resume as decisões, atribui responsáveis e fixa os prazos para as pendências.
lessons.context: Here is a short recap of our meeting. It was agreed that Racional will send the report by Friday. Two items are still pending: the steel quote and the safety plan. The owner of the steel quote is Fabio, with a due date of next Monday. I will follow up to close out the open items.

vocab.example: I will send the minutes today.
Here is a short summary.
It was agreed that we start in May.
We made one clear decision.
Two items are still pending.
We have three open items.
The owner of this task is Fabio.
The due date is next Monday.
I am in charge of procurement.
We will close out the open items.
One payment is still outstanding.
We assign an owner to each item.
Here is a quick recap.
As a follow-up, I will send the dates.

exercises.title: 1. Ditado: registre a decisão e o prazo
exercises.correctText: It was agreed that Racional will send the report by Friday.
exercises.explanation: Ouça e escreva. 'It was agreed that' (passado, a decisão) + 'will send by Friday' (futuro, o prazo): a fórmula da ata.

exercises.title: 2. Monte a frase da pendência
exercises.explanation: "This item is still pending" aponta a pendência com clareza. Depois de montar, leia em voz alta e some 'the owner is...'.

exercises.title: 3. Comunique a ata em voz alta
exercises.targetText: Here is a short recap. It was agreed that we will send the report by Friday. Two items are still pending, and I will follow up to close them out.
exercises.translation: Aqui está um resumo rápido. Ficou acordado que enviaremos o relatório até sexta. Dois itens continuam pendentes, e eu vou dar retorno para fechá-los.
exercises.prompt: Leia em voz alta como se apresentasse a ata da reunião com a Amazon: resumo, decisão com prazo e pendências a fechar.
exercises.explanation: Recap + decisão com prazo + pendências e retorno. Treine com o professor até comunicar a ata com naturalidade e firmeza.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, dê a recapitulação da reunião com a Amazon: resuma o que foi decidido, diga quem é o responsável por cada pendência e o prazo, e prometa fechar os itens em aberto. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can recap a meeting with 'Here is a short summary.'
I can record a decision with 'It was agreed that...'
I can point out an open item and its owner and due date.
I can follow up to close out the pending items.

lessons.title: Briefing & estrutura: revisão de linguagem para a Apresentação 1
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você organiza uma apresentação institucional em três blocos — abertura, corpo e fechamento — e usa os conectores de sinalização (signposting) que guiam o cliente de um ponto ao próximo.
lessons.overview:
Module 7 closes the course with three real presentations, led by you, the operations director, for three big data clients. The first is Racional's pitch (institutional presentation) to Microsoft: telling who the company is, what it delivers and why it is the right partner for a data center. Today, on the Monday briefing (preparation), you build the blueprint for this presentation before going to the job site on Friday.

Every good presentation has the same structure, and that is why it can be learned like an engineering rule. There are three blocks: the opening, where you say who you are and what you will cover; the body, with at most three points; and the closing, with a short summary and the next step. For Racional, these three points are usually history and scale, the four-stage delivery model and the commitment to safety.

What connects the blocks are the signposting phrases: small signs like Let me start with, Moving on to and to sum up. They tell the listener from Microsoft where they are on your map. The person who signposts the way seems to be in control, even with simple English, and that is exactly what you want to convey to a client of this size.
lessons.intro:
Hoje a planta é a regra do signposting. Decore quatro placas: "Today I'll walk you through three things." (abertura) · "Let me start with..." (primeiro ponto) · "Moving on to..." (transição) · "To sum up..." (fechamento).

A regra de ouro: anuncie cada bloco antes de entrar nele. Primeiro a placa, depois o conteúdo.
lessons.situation: Na segunda anterior à apresentação, você monta o esqueleto do pitch institucional da Racional para a Microsoft: o que dizer na abertura, quais três pontos no corpo e como fechar.
lessons.context: Good morning, everyone, and thank you for your time. Today I'll walk you through three things: who Racional is, what we deliver, and why we are the right partner. Let me start with our history. Then I'll move on to our delivery model. Finally, I'll close with our work on safety. To sum up, we are a reliable partner, and we hope to build something great together.

vocab.example: Today I'll walk you through our company.
Here is the agenda for today.
Let me start with our history.
Moving on to our delivery model.
Finally, I'll talk about safety.
To sum up, we are a reliable partner.
My first key point is reliability.
I want to highlight our track record.
Let me give you a quick overview.
Today I'll focus on three points.
Let's agree on the next step.
I'll close with our proposal.
We have a strong track record.
We are a reliable partner.

exercises.title: 1. Qual frase abre o corpo?
exercises.prompt: Você terminou a abertura e vai entrar no primeiro ponto. Qual signposting é o mais natural?

options.text: Let me start with our history.
That's all from me, thank you.
options.whyWrong: Isso é fechamento, não abertura do corpo. Você ainda vai apresentar os pontos.
Ordem das palavras incorreta. A estrutura é 'Let me start with' + complemento.

exercises.explanation: 'Let me start with...' anuncia o primeiro ponto do corpo e mostra que você está conduzindo o mapa.

exercises.title: 2. Sinalize o resumo final
exercises.prompt: Para fechar resumindo em uma frase: "To ___ up, Racional is a reliable partner."
exercises.explanation: 'To sum up' (ou 'to wrap up') sinaliza ao ouvinte que você vai resumir e fechar.

commonErrors.summary: 'Summary' é o substantivo. A expressão fixa é 'to sum up'.
commonErrors.end: 'To end up' tem outro sentido (acabar/parar em). Para resumir use 'to sum up'.

exercises.title: 3. Monte a frase de agenda
exercises.explanation: 'Today I'll walk you through our company' é a frase de abertura que anuncia o roteiro inteiro.

exercises.title: 4. Combine o bloco com a frase

pairs.right: Today I'll walk you through three things.
Let me start with our history.
Moving on to our delivery model.
To sum up, we are a reliable partner.

exercises.explanation: Cada bloco tem uma frase-âncora de sinalização. Decorar as quatro já dá o esqueleto inteiro do pitch.

exercises.title: 5. Seu esqueleto de abertura (2 frases)
exercises.prompt: Escreva a abertura do pitch para a Microsoft em 2 frases: (1) um cumprimento + anúncio do roteiro e (2) o anúncio do primeiro ponto. Use ao menos 2 termos em inglês desta lição. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
keywords: let me start with|key point|highlight|track record
exercises.modelAnswer: Good morning, and thank you for your time. Today I'll walk you through three things, and let me start with our track record.
exercises.explanation: Abertura que anuncia o roteiro mais o primeiro signposting. Em duas frases o ouvinte já sabe para onde você o leva.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, anuncie o roteiro de uma apresentação sua em três pontos, usando 'First..., then..., finally...'. Sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can structure a presentation into opening, body, and closing.
I can announce my agenda with 'Today I'll walk you through...'.
I can signpost each section with 'Let me start with' and 'Moving on to'.
I can guide my listener through the talk like a clear map.

watch: Priorize a FALA: o aluno deve falar na maior parte da aula.
Varie a dinâmica a cada aula — o roteiro acima rotaciona para não repetir.
Não deixar a teoria virar palestra: o aluno tem que produzir.
Conectar a regra a uma fala real do cliente.

lessons.title: Apresentação 1 — Pitch institucional Racional para a Microsoft
lessons.objective: Ao final desta aula você ensaia e entrega o pitch institucional completo da Racional para a Microsoft — abertura, corpo em três pontos e fechamento com próximo passo.
lessons.overview:
Today is the job site: you deliver, you do not plan. On the Friday capstone (final delivery), you lead Racional's pitch (institutional presentation) to Microsoft, from start to finish, with the teacher in the role of the client. It is the first of the three big presentations that close the course.

The business goal is clear: to create trust. Microsoft builds extremely demanding data centers, and it wants a solid partner. You show this with simple facts, founded in 1971, more than 620 projects and ten million square meters built, and with the four-stage delivery model, from start to finish, always to control quality.

Use the map you built on Monday: opening with the agenda, three points in the body (history and scale, delivery model, safety) and a closing with a concrete next step, inviting them to a technical visit. A presentation that does not ask for action was just a talk; yours ends by asking for the next step.
lessons.intro:
Sem teoria nova hoje. Retome as placas de sinalização e fixe três frases-âncora do pitch.

"Founded in 1971, Racional has delivered over 620 projects." · "We work from start to finish, so we control quality." · "We'd be proud to be your partner. Could we schedule a visit?"
lessons.situation: Reunião institucional com a Microsoft. Você tem cinco minutos para apresentar a Racional e conquistar a confiança para um futuro projeto de data center.
lessons.context: Good morning, and thank you for having us. Today I'll walk you through who we are. Founded in 1971, Racional has delivered over 620 projects and more than ten million square meters built. We work in four stages, from start to finish, so we control quality at every step. Safety comes first on every site. To sum up, we'd be proud to be your partner on your next data center. Could we schedule a technical visit as the next step? We really look forward to working with you.

vocab.example: Thank you for having us today.
Racional was founded in 1971.
We have ten million square meters built.
We deliver projects on time.
We work in four stages.
We follow the project from start to finish.
We control quality at every step.
We have expertise in large projects.
We are proud to work with you.
We want to build trust with our clients.
Can we schedule a visit next week?
Our experience is added value for you.
You need a strong partner. That's where we come in.
We look forward to working with you.

exercises.title: 1. Como abrir o pitch com a Microsoft?
exercises.prompt: O cliente acabou de recebê-lo na sala. Qual é a abertura mais natural e profissional?

options.text: Thank you for having us. Today I'll walk you through who we are.
Having us thank you. Walk who we are.
options.whyWrong: Ordem das palavras quebrada. As expressões fixas são 'Thank you for having us' e 'walk you through'.

options.text: We can go now to the price, please.
options.whyWrong: Pular direto para preço quebra a confiança. Primeiro abertura e história; preço é outra apresentação.

exercises.explanation: 'Thank you for having us' + 'Today I'll walk you through...' abre com cortesia e já anuncia o roteiro.

exercises.title: 2. Escreva o corpo do pitch (3 frases)
exercises.prompt: Escreva o corpo do pitch para a Microsoft em 3 frases curtas: história/escala, modelo de entrega e segurança. Use ao menos 3 termos em inglês desta lição. A correção é só sobre o uso dos termos.
exercises.modelAnswer: Racional was founded in 1971 and has delivered over 620 projects. We work from start to finish, so we control quality at every stage. We are proud to build trust with strong partners like you.
exercises.explanation: Três frases, três pontos. Cada uma usa um termo-âncora e mantém o inglês simples e direto.

exercises.title: 3. Feche o pitch em voz alta
exercises.prompt: Leia o fechamento do pitch para a Microsoft, devagar, terminando com o próximo passo.
exercises.targetText: To sum up, we'd be proud to be your partner. Could we schedule a technical visit as the next step?
exercises.translation: Resumindo, teríamos orgulho de ser seu parceiro. Poderíamos agendar uma visita técnica como próximo passo?
exercises.explanation: Todo fechamento termina com um pedido de ação. 'Could we schedule a visit?' abre a porta para a próxima conversa.

lessons.critical: Em voz alta, apresente a Racional para a Microsoft em quatro frases (abertura, história, entrega, próximo passo), de memória e sem texto na frente.
takeaways: I can open a pitch with 'Thank you for having us'.
I can present our history with 'founded in 1971'.
I can explain our model 'from start to finish'.
I can close with a clear next step and a visit.
I can say 'we look forward to working with you'.

teacher.focus: Demonstração integrada de domínio (avaliação).

flow.how: Aluno organiza a apresentação; cheque tempo e estrutura.
Aluno conduz o cenário do início ao fim, em inglês.
Avalie clareza, fluência, vocabulário e domínio; grave.

watch: Priorize a FALA: o aluno deve falar na maior parte da aula.
Varie a dinâmica a cada aula — o roteiro acima rotaciona para não repetir.
Avaliar com critérios claros; gravar para devolutiva.
